at kalde.explanation: "At kalde" means "to call", as in giving a name. To name someone or something, say: "Vi kalder hunden Max" (We call the dog Max). For phoning, use "at ringe" (to phone): "Jeg ringer til dig" (I will call you).

sentence.da: Vi vil **kalde** vores baby Emma.
sentence.en: We want to call our baby Emma.

at kalde på.explanation: "At kalde på" means "to call for". To call out so that someone comes, add the person after "på" (on): "Han kalder på sin mor" (He calls for his mother). Without "på", "at kalde" means to name. For example, "Vi kalder hunden Max" (We call the dog Max).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **kalde på** tjeneren, når vi skal betale.
sentence.en: I will call for the waiter when we want to pay.

at kaste.explanation: "At kaste" means "to throw". To throw something to someone, add "til" (to): "Jeg kaster bolden til dig" (I throw the ball to you). With "op" (up), it means "to vomit". For example, "Jeg skal kaste op" (I am going to be sick).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **kaste** sten i vandet.
sentence.en: The children want to throw stones into the water.

at kaste håndklædet i ringen.explanation: "At kaste håndklædet i ringen" means "to give up". Literally, it is "to throw the towel in the ring". For a plain way to say it, use "at give op" (to give up): "Jeg giver op" (I give up).

forms.da: Vi vil ikke kaste håndklædet i ringen

sentence.da: Efter tre nederlag vil han **kaste håndklædet i ringen**.
sentence.en: After three defeats, he wants to throw in the towel.

at kaste op.explanation: "At kaste op" means "to throw up". It is built from "kaste" (to throw) and "op" (up). Without "op", "kaste" means to throw an object. For example, "Jeg kaster bolden" (I throw the ball).

sentence.da: Han er syg og vil **kaste op**.
sentence.en: He is sick and wants to throw up.

at kategorisere.explanation: "At kategorisere" means "to categorize". It comes from "en kategori" (a category).

sentence.da: Biblioteket vil **kategorisere** bøgerne efter emne.
sentence.en: The library wants to categorize the books by topic.

at kede sig.explanation: "At kede sig" means "to be bored". To say you are bored, use "mig" (myself): "Jeg keder mig" (I am bored). The small word "sig" (oneself) changes with the person. For example, "Han keder sig" (He is bored), "Vi keder os" (We are bored).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **kede sig**, når de ikke har legetøj.
sentence.en: The children can get bored when they have no toys.

at kende.explanation: "At kende" means "to know", as in being familiar with a person or a place. For example, "Jeg kender Anna" (I know Anna). To know a fact, use "at vide" (to know): "Jeg ved, at hun bor her" (I know that she lives here).

forms.en: I have known (a person or place)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **kende** dine venner bedre.
sentence.en: I would like to know your friends better.

at kidnappe.explanation: "At kidnappe" means "to kidnap". The person who does it is "en kidnapper" (a kidnapper). For example, "Politiet leder efter kidnapperen" (The police are looking for the kidnapper).

sentence.da: De vil **kidnappe** hende og kræve penge.
sentence.en: They want to kidnap her and demand money.

at kigge.explanation: "At kigge" means "to look". To tell someone to look, say: "Kig her!" (Look here!). To say what you look at, add "på" (at): "Jeg kigger på billedet" (I am looking at the picture). To tell a shop assistant you do not need help, say: "Jeg kigger bare" (I'm just looking).

sentence.da: Jeg vil bare **kigge** på tøjet i butikken.
sentence.en: I just want to look at the clothes in the store.

at kigge efter.explanation: "At kigge efter" means "to look for". To say what you are searching for, put it after "efter" (for): "Jeg kigger efter mine briller" (I am looking for my glasses). When you watch over someone, it means "to keep an eye on": "Kig efter børnene" (Keep an eye on the kids).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **kigge efter** mine nøgler i bilen.
sentence.en: I have to look for my keys in the car.

at kildre.explanation: "At kildre" means "to tickle". To say you tickle someone, name the person after it: "Han kildrede mig på foden" (He tickled me on the foot). To say a spot feels ticklish, use "det kildrer" (it tickles): "Det kildrer i næsen" (My nose tickles).

sentence.da: Han griner, når jeg vil **kildre** ham.
sentence.en: He laughs when I want to tickle him.

at klage.explanation: "At klage" means "to complain". To name the topic of the complaint, add "over" (about): "Han klager over støjen" (He is complaining about the noise). To name the person or organization you complain to, add "til" (to): "Jeg klager til banken" (I am complaining to the bank).

related.en: a formal complaint about a product

sentence.da: Jeg vil **klage** over den kolde mad.
sentence.en: I will complain about the cold food.

at klappe.explanation: "At klappe" means "to clap or pat". To show you liked a show, clap your hands: "Publikum klapper" (The audience claps). To stroke a pet gently, pat it: "Jeg klapper hunden" (I pat the dog).

sentence.da: Alle vil **klappe**, når sangeren er færdig.
sentence.en: Everyone will clap when the singer is done.

at klare.explanation: "At klare" means "to manage or cope". To say you handle a task, say: "Han klarer opgaven" (He manages the task). To say you pass a test, say: "Jeg klarede prøven" (I passed the test).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt **klare** den opgave alene.
sentence.en: I can handle that task on my own.

at klare op.explanation: "At klare op" means "to clear up", for weather that gets better. For example, "Det klarer op i aften" (It will clear up this evening). For tidying a room, use "at rydde op" (to tidy up) instead: "Jeg rydder op på værelset" (I tidy up the room).

sentence.da: Jeg håber, det vil **klare op** i morgen.
sentence.en: I hope it will clear up tomorrow.

at klare sig.explanation: "At klare sig" means "to get by or do well". To say someone is doing well in a place, say: "Hun klarer sig fint i Danmark" (She is doing fine in Denmark). To say you manage without something, add "uden" (without): "Jeg klarer mig uden bil" (I get by without a car).

forms.en: I have gotten by / done well

sentence.da: Hun er voksen og kan **klare sig** selv.
sentence.en: She is grown up and can take care of herself.

at klassificere.explanation: "At klassificere" means "to classify". It comes from "en klasse" (a class).

sentence.da: Forskerne vil **klassificere** planterne efter deres blade.
sentence.en: The scientists want to classify the plants by their leaves.

at klatre.explanation: "At klatre" means "to climb", as in going up with hands and feet. To say children climb a tree, say: "Børnene klatrer i et træ" (The children climb a tree). To say prices go up, use the same verb: "Priserne klatrer" (Prices are climbing).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **klatre** op i det høje træ.
sentence.en: I want to climb up the tall tree.

at klemme.explanation: "At klemme" means "to squeeze or pinch". To say your finger got caught in a door, say: "Jeg klemte fingeren i døren" (I pinched my finger in the door).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **klemme** en citron over fisken.
sentence.en: I want to squeeze a lemon over the fish.

at klikke.explanation: "At klikke" means "to click". To name the item you click, add "på" (on) before the item: "Jeg klikker på linket" (I click on the link). To click twice quickly, use "at dobbeltklikke" (to double-click): "Dobbeltklik på ikonet" (Double-click the icon).

sentence.da: Du skal **klikke** på den blå knap.
sentence.en: You have to click on the blue button.

at klippe.explanation: "At klippe" means "to cut (with scissors)". To cut paper with scissors, say: "Jeg klipper papir" (I cut paper). To say a hairdresser cuts hair, use the same verb: "Hun klipper mit hår" (She cuts my hair).

sentence.da: Hun vil **klippe** mit hår i morgen.
sentence.en: She will cut my hair tomorrow.

at klynge sig.explanation: "At klynge sig" means "to cling". To say what you cling to, add "til" (to): "Han klynger sig til rækværket" (He clings to the railing). The same pattern works for feelings. For example, "Hun klynger sig til håbet" (She clings to hope).

sentence.da: Barnet vil **klynge sig** til sin mor, når det er bange.
sentence.en: The child will cling to its mother when it is scared.

at klæde.explanation: "At klæde" means "to suit". To say a color or clothes look good on someone, put the person after the verb: "Blåt klæder hende" (Blue suits her). With "sig" (oneself) it means dressing yourself. For example, "Jeg klæder mig på" (I get dressed).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, at den røde kjole vil **klæde** dig.
sentence.en: I think the red dress will suit you.

at klæde sig af.explanation: "At klæde sig af" means "to get undressed". The small word after "klæde" changes with the person. For example, "Jeg klæder mig af" (I get undressed), "Hun klæder sig af" (She gets undressed). The opposite is "at klæde sig på" (to get dressed). For another example, "Jeg klæder mig på" (I get dressed).

sentence.da: Barnet skal **klæde sig af** og tage et bad.
sentence.en: The child has to get undressed and take a bath.

at klæde sig på.explanation: "At klæde sig på" means "to get dressed". The small word "sig" (oneself) changes with the person. For example, "Du klæder dig på" (You get dressed), "Han klæder sig på" (He gets dressed). To put on one item, say "at tage en jakke på" (to put on a jacket): "Jeg tager jakken på" (I put on the jacket).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **klæde sig på** nu.
sentence.en: The children have to get dressed now.

at klø.explanation: "At klø" means "to itch or scratch". To say something itches, say: "Det klør" (It itches). To scratch yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Jeg klør mig i hovedet" (I scratch my head).

sentence.da: Huden kan **klø**, når en myg har stukket dig.
sentence.en: Your skin can itch when a mosquito has bitten you.

at klø sig.explanation: "At klø sig" means "to scratch oneself". It is built from "at klø" (to itch / scratch) and "sig" (oneself). To name the body part you scratch, add "på" (on) before it: "Jeg klør mig på ryggen" (I scratch my back).

sentence.da: Hunden vil **klø sig** bag øret med poten.
sentence.en: The dog wants to scratch itself behind the ear with its paw.

at knappe.explanation: "At knappe" means "to button". To say what you button, name it after the verb: "Han knapper skjorten" (He buttons the shirt). To open the buttons again, add "op" (up): "Jeg knapper jakken op" (I unbutton the jacket).

sentence.da: Du skal **knappe** frakken, fordi det er koldt.
sentence.en: You must button the coat because it is cold.

at knibe.explanation: "At knibe" means "to pinch or squint". To say someone pinched you, say: "Hun kneb mig i armen" (She pinched my arm). To say someone squints, add "øjnene sammen" (the eyes together): "Han kniber øjnene sammen" (He squints). When money is short, say: "Det kniber med pengene" (Money is tight).

sentence.da: Man må **knibe** øjnene sammen, når solen skinner kraftigt.
sentence.en: You have to squint when the sun shines strongly.

at knuse.explanation: "At knuse" means "to crush". To say something broke into pieces, like glass, say: "Han knuste glasset" (He smashed the glass). It also works for feelings. For example, "Det knuste hendes hjerte" (It broke her heart).

sentence.da: Hun vil **knuse** nødderne med en hammer.
sentence.en: She wants to crush the nuts with a hammer.

at knytte.explanation: "At knytte" means "to tie or connect". To clench a fist, say: "Han knytter næven" (He clenches his fist). To form a friendship, say: "De knytter et venskab" (They form a friendship). For tying shoelaces, use "at binde" (to tie): "Jeg binder mine snørebånd" (I tie my shoelaces).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **knytte** rebet fast, fordi båden driver væk.
sentence.en: I must tie the rope fast because the boat is drifting away.

at knække.explanation: "At knække" means "to crack or break". To say you break a stick, say: "Jeg knækker en pind" (I break a stick). For a broken bone, use "at brække" (to break): "Jeg har brækket armen" (I have broken my arm).

sentence.da: Man skal **knække** skallen for at spise nødden.
sentence.en: To eat the nut, you must crack the shell.

at knæle.explanation: "At knæle" means "to kneel". It comes from "et knæ" (a knee). To say someone proposed on one knee, say: "Han knælede og friede" (He knelt and proposed).

sentence.da: Man kan **knæle**, så begge knæ rører gulvet.
sentence.en: You can kneel so that both knees touch the floor.

at koge.explanation: "At koge" means "to boil". To say water is bubbling hot, say: "Vandet koger" (The water is boiling). To boil food in water, name the food: "Jeg koger æg" (I boil eggs). For making a meal, use "at lave mad" (to cook): "Jeg laver mad" (I am cooking).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **koge** kartofler i vand.
sentence.en: I am going to boil potatoes in water.

at koge over.explanation: "At koge over" means "to boil over". To say milk runs out of the pot, say: "Mælken koger over" (The milk boils over). It also works for feelings. For example, "Hun koger over af vrede" (She is boiling over with anger).

sentence.da: Mælken kan **koge over**, når du ikke passer på.
sentence.en: The milk can boil over when you are not watching.

at kollidere.explanation: "At kollidere" means "to collide". To name what you hit, add "med" (with): "Bilen kolliderede med en cykel" (The car collided with a bicycle). When two plans clash, use the same verb: "Mødet kolliderer med min tandlægetid" (The meeting clashes with my dentist appointment).

sentence.da: To biler kan **kollidere**, når vejen er glat.
sentence.en: Two cars can collide when the road is slippery.

at kombinere.explanation: "At kombinere" means "to combine". To say which things you put together, join them with "med" (with): "Du kan kombinere en rød trøje med sorte bukser" (You can combine a red sweater with black trousers).

sentence.da: Du kan **kombinere** ris og grøntsager.
sentence.en: You can combine rice and vegetables.

at komme.explanation: "At komme" means "to come". To say you are on your way, say: "Jeg kommer nu" (I am coming now). To ask where someone is from, use it with "fra" (from): "Hvor kommer du fra?" (Where are you from?). To say what will happen next, use "kommer til at": "Det kommer til at regne" (It is going to rain).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme** til din fest i morgen.
sentence.en: I will come to your party tomorrow.

at komme an på.explanation: "At komme an på" means "to depend on". To answer a yes-or-no question when it is not clear, say: "Kommer du?" "Det kommer an på" (Are you coming? It depends). To name what it depends on, add it after "på" (on): "Det kommer an på prisen" (It depends on the price).

sentence.da: Det vil **komme an på** vejret i morgen.
sentence.en: It will depend on the weather tomorrow.

at komme for sent.explanation: "At komme for sent" means "to be late". Literally, it is "to come too late". To say you were late, say: "Jeg kom for sent til skolen" (I was late for school). For a train or bus, use "forsinket" (delayed): "Toget er forsinket" (The train is delayed).

forms.en: I have been late / arrived late

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **komme for sent** til mødet.
sentence.en: I do not want to be late for the meeting.

at komme forbi.explanation: "At komme forbi" means "to come by". To invite someone to drop in for a visit, say: "Kom forbi i aften" (Come by tonight). To say you cannot pass something in the way, use it for "get past": "Vi kan ikke komme forbi bilen" (We cannot get past the car).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **komme forbi** i morgen.
sentence.en: You are welcome to come by tomorrow.

at komme frem.explanation: "At komme frem" means "to arrive or come forward". To say when a trip ended, say: "Vi kom frem klokken seks" (We arrived at six o'clock). To say someone stepped forward, say: "Han kom frem fra mængden" (He came forward from the crowd).

sentence.da: Toget skal **komme frem** klokken seks.
sentence.en: The train is due to arrive at six o'clock.

at komme godt ud af det med.explanation: "At komme godt ud af det med" means "to get along with". To say you have a good relationship with someone, say: "Jeg kommer godt ud af det med min chef" (I get along well with my boss). Put "dårligt" (badly) in place of "godt" (well) to say the opposite: "Jeg kommer dårligt ud af det med min nabo" (I get along badly with my neighbor).

forms.da: at komme godt ud af det med
jeg kommer godt ud af det med
jeg kom godt ud af det med
jeg er kommet godt ud af det med

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **komme godt ud af det med** mine nye kolleger.
sentence.en: I would like to get along well with my new colleagues.

at komme hjem.explanation: "At komme hjem" means "to come home". To ask when someone gets home, say: "Hvornår kommer du hjem?" (When will you get home?). To say you are setting off for home, use "at tage hjem" (to go home): "Jeg tager hjem nu" (I am going home now).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme hjem** i aften.
sentence.en: I want to come home tonight.

at komme i gang.explanation: "At komme i gang" means "to get started". To name the task you start, add "med" (with) and the task: "Jeg kom i gang med opgaven" (I got started on the task).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **komme i gang** med arbejdet.
sentence.en: I would like to get started on the work.

at komme i tanke om.explanation: "At komme i tanke om" means "to remember or think of". To say a thing suddenly came back to you, say: "Jeg kom i tanke om nøglerne" (I remembered the keys). To say you simply keep something in memory, use "at huske" (to remember): "Jeg husker hans navn" (I remember his name).

forms.da: jeg er kommet i tanke om

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **komme i tanke om** hans navn.
sentence.en: I can't think of his name.

at komme ind.explanation: "At komme ind" means "to come in". To invite someone into a room, say: "Kom ind!" (Come in!). To say you could not get into a place, say: "Vi kom ikke ind i klubben" (We could not get into the club).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **komme ind** uden nøgle.
sentence.en: I cannot get in without a key.

at komme med.explanation: "At komme med" means "to come along or bring". To ask if someone joins you, say: "Kommer du med?" (Are you coming along?). To say someone brought something, say: "Hun kom med kage" (She brought cake).

sentence.da: Vil du **komme med** i biografen i aften?
sentence.en: Do you want to come along to the movies tonight?

at komme ned.explanation: "At komme ned" means "to come down". To tell someone to come down from a high place, say: "Kom ned derfra!" (Come down from there!).

sentence.da: Kan du **komme ned** af trappen?
sentence.en: Can you come down the stairs?

at komme op.explanation: "At komme op" means "to come up or get up". To invite someone upstairs, say: "Kom op til os!" (Come up to us!). To push someone to try harder, say: "Kom op!" (Come on!). To get out of bed, use "at stå op" (to get up): "Jeg står op klokken syv" (I get up at seven).

forms.en: I have come up / gotten up

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **komme op** af stolen.
sentence.en: I cannot get up from the chair.

at komme over.explanation: "At komme over" means "to get over". To say someone never recovered from something hard, say: "Han kom aldrig over det" (He never got over it). To invite someone to visit you, say: "Kom over til os!" (Come over to our place!).

sentence.da: Det tager tid at **komme over** en stor sorg.
sentence.en: It takes time to get over great sorrow.

at komme sig.explanation: "At komme sig" means "to recover". It is built from "at komme" (to come) and "sig" (oneself). To name what you recover from, add "efter" (after): "Jeg kommer mig efter sygdommen" (I am recovering from the illness).

sentence.da: Efter operationen skal han **komme sig** i to uger.
sentence.en: After the surgery, he has to recover for two weeks.

at komme til skade.explanation: "At komme til skade" means "to get hurt". To say when someone got hurt, say: "Han kom til skade i går" (He got hurt yesterday). To name the body part, add "på" (on) before it: "Jeg kom til skade på benet" (I hurt my leg).

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **komme til skade** på isen.
sentence.en: The children must not get hurt on the ice.

at komme tilbage.explanation: "At komme tilbage" means "to come back". To say you will return soon, say: "Jeg kommer snart tilbage" (I will be back soon). The word "tilbage" (back) is also in "at give tilbage" (to give back) and "at betale tilbage" (to pay back).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme tilbage** til Danmark næste år.
sentence.en: I want to come back to Denmark next year.

at komme ud.explanation: "At komme ud" means "to come out or get out". To tell someone to leave a room, say: "Kom ud!" (Come out!). To say where someone comes out of, add "af" (of): "Han kommer ud af skolen" (He comes out of the school).

forms.en: I have come out / gotten out

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme ud** af huset.
sentence.en: I want to get out of the house.

at komme videre.explanation: "At komme videre" means "to move on". To say you want to leave something painful behind, say: "Jeg vil gerne komme videre efter bruddet" (I want to move on after the breakup). To say you continue a trip, say: "Vi kom videre til næste by" (We went on to the next town).

sentence.da: Vi bliver ikke her, men vil **komme videre** i dag.
sentence.en: We are not staying here, but want to move on today.

at kommentere.explanation: "At kommentere" means "to comment". To say what you comment on, put it right after the verb, with no word for "on": "Hun kommenterer videoen" (She is commenting on the video).

sentence.da: Politikeren ville ikke **kommentere** sagen til pressen.
sentence.en: The politician did not want to comment on the case to the press.

at kommunikere.explanation: "At kommunikere" means "to communicate". To say which language you use, add "på" (in): "Vi kommunikerer på dansk" (We communicate in Danish). To name the person you communicate with, add "med" (with): "Jeg kommunikerer med kunden" (I communicate with the customer).

sentence.da: Vi kan **kommunikere** på engelsk og dansk.
sentence.en: We can communicate in English and Danish.

at kompensere.explanation: "At kompensere" means "to compensate". To name what you make up for, add "for" (for) before it: "Jeg kompenserer for fejlen" (I compensate for the mistake).

sentence.da: Han vil **kompensere** for sin højde med hurtige fødder.
sentence.en: He wants to compensate for his height with fast feet.

at komplicere.explanation: "At komplicere" means "to complicate". To say something makes matters harder, add "tingene" (the things): "Det komplicerer tingene" (That complicates things).

sentence.da: Nye regler kan **komplicere** en opgave, der var nem før.
sentence.en: New rules can complicate a task that used to be easy.

at komponere.explanation: "At komponere" means "to compose". To say who writes the music and who plays it, say: "Hun komponerer, og han spiller" (She composes and he plays).

sentence.da: Hun vil **komponere** musik til en film.
sentence.en: She wants to compose music for a film.

at koncentrere sig.explanation: "At koncentrere sig" means "to concentrate". To say you cannot focus, say: "Jeg kan ikke koncentrere mig" (I cannot concentrate). To name the task you focus on, add "om" (on) before the task: "Vi koncentrerer os om opgaven" (We are concentrating on the task).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **koncentrere sig**, når der er larm.
sentence.en: It is hard to concentrate when there is noise.

at konfirmere.explanation: "At konfirmere" means "to confirm", in the church ceremony where a young person confirms their baptism. In Denmark, the confirmation is followed by a family party called "en konfirmationsfest". To say you have been confirmed, say: "Jeg er konfirmeret" (I am confirmed).

sentence.da: Præsten vil **konfirmere** de unge i kirken i maj.
sentence.en: The priest will confirm the young people in the church in May.

at konkludere.explanation: "At konkludere" means "to conclude". To state the conclusion, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg konkluderer, at planen virker" (I conclude that the plan works).

sentence.da: Efter testen kan vi **konkludere**, at medicinen virker.
sentence.en: After the test we can conclude that the medicine works.

at konkurrere.explanation: "At konkurrere" means "to compete". To say who you compete with, add "med" (with): "Jeg konkurrerer med min bror" (I compete with my brother). To name the prize, add "om" (for): "Vi konkurrerer om prisen" (We compete for the prize).

sentence.da: Mange firmaer vil **konkurrere** om de samme kunder.
sentence.en: Many companies compete for the same customers.

at konstatere.explanation: "At konstatere" means "to state or establish". To report a fact you have just seen or checked, follow it with "at" (that) and the fact: "Politiet konstaterede, at ingen var kommet til skade" (The police established that nobody had been hurt).

sentence.da: Jeg må **konstatere**, at vi ikke har nok penge.
sentence.en: I have to state that we do not have enough money.

at konstruere.explanation: "At konstruere" means "to construct". To say you design and build something with a plan, put the thing after it: "at konstruere en maskine" (to construct a machine).

sentence.da: Ingeniøren skal **konstruere** en bro over fjorden.
sentence.en: The engineer is going to construct a bridge over the fjord.

at kontakte.explanation: "At kontakte" means "to contact". It is built from "en kontakt" (a contact). To say you will get in touch with a bank, put the bank right after it: "Jeg kontakter banken i morgen" (I will contact the bank tomorrow).

sentence.da: Du kan **kontakte** lægen på telefon.
sentence.en: You can contact the doctor by phone.

at kontrollere.explanation: "At kontrollere" means "to check or inspect". It is built from the noun "en kontrol" (a check). To say officials look at something, put the thing after it: "Politiet kontrollerer bilerne" (The police check the cars).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **kontrollere** tallene en gang til.
sentence.en: I want to check the numbers once more.

at koordinere.explanation: "At koordinere" means "to coordinate". The person who does it is "en koordinator" (a coordinator). To say you arrange a meeting between people, put the meeting after it: "Jeg koordinerer mødet med kunderne" (I coordinate the meeting with the customers).

sentence.da: Hun skal **koordinere** arbejdet mellem de tre hold.
sentence.en: She is going to coordinate the work between the three teams.

at kopiere.explanation: "At kopiere" means "to copy". To say you copy a file on a computer: "Jeg kopierer filen" (I copy the file). To ask someone to photocopy pages: "Kan du kopiere de her sider?" (Can you copy these pages?)

sentence.da: Kan du **kopiere** de her papirer til mig?
sentence.en: Can you copy these papers for me?

at korrigere.explanation: "At korrigere" means "to correct". To say you fix a mistake in a report, put the thing you fix after it: "Jeg korrigerer tallet i rapporten" (I correct the number in the report). To say someone is right, do not use "at korrigere"; use "at have ret" (to be right): "Du har ret" (You are right).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **korrigere** vores fejl i opgaven.
sentence.en: The teacher will correct our mistakes in the assignment.

at kortlægge.explanation: "At kortlægge" means "to map". It is built from "et kort" (a map) and "at lægge" (to put). To say you find out and list the facts about a problem, put the problem after it: "at kortlægge problemet" (to map out the problem).

sentence.da: Forskerne vil **kortlægge**, hvordan sygdommen spreder sig.
sentence.en: The researchers want to map how the disease spreads.

at koste.explanation: "At koste" means "to cost". To ask a price, use "det" (it): "Hvad koster det?" (How much does it cost?). The forms above start with "det" (it) instead of "jeg" (I), because a thing, not a person, does the costing.

sentence.da: Den nye bluse vil **koste** hundrede kroner.
sentence.en: The new blouse will cost a hundred kroner.

at kramme.explanation: "At kramme" means "to hug". To ask for a hug, use the noun "et kram" (a hug): "Giv mig et kram!" (Give me a hug!)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **kramme** min mor, fordi jeg savner hende.
sentence.en: I want to hug my mom because I miss her.

at kravle.explanation: "At kravle" means "to crawl". To say a baby moves on hands and knees: "Babyen kravler på gulvet" (The baby crawls on the floor). To say someone goes up using hands and feet: "Han kravler op i træet" (He crawls up the tree).

sentence.da: Min lille søn kan **kravle** meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: My little son can crawl very fast.

at kritisere.explanation: "At kritisere" means "to criticize". To say what you criticize someone for, use "for" (for): "Han kritiserede hende for fejlen" (He criticized her for the mistake).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **kritisere** mit forslag.
sentence.en: You are welcome to criticize my suggestion.

at krybe.explanation: "At krybe" means "to creep or crawl". To say a child goes low under something: "Barnet kryber ind under bordet" (The child crawls in under the table). A reptile is "et krybdyr", built from "at krybe" and "et dyr" (an animal).

sentence.da: Slangen kan **krybe** ind under den store sten.
sentence.en: The snake can creep in under the big stone.

at krydre.explanation: "At krydre" means "to season". It comes from "et krydderi" (a spice). To name the spice you season with, add "med" (with) before it: "at krydre med chili" (to season with chili).

sentence.da: Man skal **krydre** suppen med salt og peber.
sentence.en: You have to season the soup with salt and pepper.

at krydse.explanation: "At krydse" means "to cross". It comes from "et kryds" (a cross). To say you pass over a border: "Vi krydser grænsen i morgen" (We cross the border tomorrow).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **krydse** gaden, når lyset er grønt.
sentence.en: The children must cross the street when the light is green.

at kræve.explanation: "At kræve" means "to require". To say what a task needs: "Opgaven kræver tid" (The task requires time). A different use is "to demand", when you insist on something: "Han kræver svar" (He demands an answer).

sentence.da: Det nye job vil **kræve** meget tid.
sentence.en: The new job will require a lot of time.

at kunne.explanation: "At kunne" means "to be able to". To say you are able to do something, put the verb right after "kan", with no "at" (to): "Jeg kan svømme" (I can swim). To ask someone for help: "Kan du hjælpe mig?" (Can you help me?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **kunne** svømme som en fisk.
sentence.en: I would like to be able to swim like a fish.

at kunne lide.explanation: "At kunne lide" means "to like". To say you like something: "Jeg kan lide kaffe" (I like coffee). To say you do not like it, put "ikke" (not) after "kan": "Jeg kan ikke lide det" (I do not like it).

sentence.da: Du vil **kunne lide** maden her.
sentence.en: You will like the food here.

at kurere.explanation: "At kurere" means "to cure". To say you cure an illness, put the illness after it: "at kurere en sygdom" (to cure a disease).

sentence.da: Lægerne håber at kunne **kurere** hende helt.
sentence.en: The doctors hope to be able to cure her completely.

at kvaje sig.explanation: "At kvaje sig" means "to mess up". To say you did something clumsy by accident: "Jeg kvajede mig og tabte kaffen" (I messed up and dropped the coffee).

sentence.da: Man kan nemt **kvaje sig**, når man er nervøs.
sentence.en: It is easy to mess up when you are nervous.

at kvalificere.explanation: "At kvalificere" means "to qualify". To say a team gets into a final, add "sig" (oneself) and "til" (to): "Holdet kvalificerer sig til finalen" (The team qualifies for the final).

sentence.da: Holdet vil **kvalificere** sig til slutspillet i år.
sentence.en: The team wants to qualify for the playoffs this year.

at kvidre.explanation: "At kvidre" means "to chirp". To say birds are making their light, high sounds: "Fuglene kvidrer i haven" (The birds are chirping in the garden).

sentence.da: Om foråret kan man høre små fugle **kvidre** i træerne.
sentence.en: In spring, you can hear small birds chirp in the trees.

at kvittere.explanation: "At kvittere" means "to acknowledge or sign for". To say you sign for a package, use "for" (for): "Jeg kvitterer for pakken" (I sign for the package). To say you thank someone for help with a gift, use "for" and "med" (with): "Hun kvitterer for hjælpen med en kage" (She thanks them for the help with a cake).

sentence.da: Jeg måtte **kvittere** for nøglen, da jeg hentede den.
sentence.en: I had to sign for the key when I picked it up.

at kvæle.explanation: "At kvæle" means "to strangle or choke". To say you stop someone from breathing, put the person after it: "Han forsøgte at kvæle ham" (He tried to strangle him). To say you stop an idea from growing: "Chefen kvæler ideen" (The boss smothers the idea).

sentence.da: Planterne vil **kvæle** hinanden, hvis de står for tæt.
sentence.en: The plants will smother each other if they stand too close.

at kysse.explanation: "At kysse" means "to kiss". To say where you kiss someone, add "på" (on) before the place: "Han kyssede hende på kinden" (He kissed her on the cheek).

sentence.da: Hun vil **kysse** sin baby godnat.
sentence.en: She wants to kiss her baby good night.

at kæle.explanation: "At kæle" means "to cuddle or pet". To name the animal or person you cuddle, add "med" (with) before it: "Hun kæler med hunden" (She cuddles the dog).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker at **kæle** med den lille kat.
sentence.en: The children love to cuddle with the little cat.

at kæmpe.explanation: "At kæmpe" means "to fight or struggle". To say a team fights hard in a match: "Holdet kæmper hårdt" (The team fights hard). To say something is difficult for you, add "med" (with): "Hun kæmper med lektierne" (She struggles with her homework). To say people argue, do not use "at kæmpe"; use "at skændes" (to argue): "Vi skændes om pengene" (We argue about the money).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **kæmpe** for mit hold.
sentence.en: I will fight for my team.

at kæmpe for.explanation: "At kæmpe for" means "to fight for". To say you work hard for something you believe in: "Vi kæmper for retfærdighed" (We fight for justice). To say a team tries hard to win: "Holdet kæmper for sejren" (The team is fighting for the win).

sentence.da: Vi må **kæmpe for** vores drømme.
sentence.en: We have to fight for our dreams.

at købe.explanation: "At købe" means "to buy". To say what you paid, add "for" (for) before the price: "Jeg købte den for hundrede kroner" (I bought it for a hundred kroner). To say who you buy something for, use "til" (to): "Jeg køber en gave til min mor" (I buy a gift for my mother).

sentence.da: Vi kan **købe** mælk i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: We can buy milk at the supermarket.

at købe ind.explanation: "At købe ind" means "to buy groceries". To say you shop for a coming weekend: "Jeg køber ind til weekenden" (I am buying groceries for the weekend). To say you buy a single item, use "at købe" (to buy): "Jeg købte en bog" (I bought a book).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **købe ind** til aftensmad.
sentence.en: I need to buy groceries for dinner.

at køre.explanation: "At køre" means "to drive". To say you go by car: "Jeg kører i bil" (I go by car). To say a bus or train runs: "Bussen kører hver time" (The bus runs every hour). To say you go by bike, use "at cykle" (to cycle): "Jeg cykler på arbejde" (I cycle to work).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **køre** bilen til arbejde i morgen.
sentence.en: I want to drive the car to work tomorrow.

at køre fast.explanation: "At køre fast" means "to get stuck". To say a car cannot move on: "Bilen kørte fast i mudderet" (The car got stuck in the mud). To say a conversation stops moving forward: "Samtalen kørte fast" (The conversation got stuck).

sentence.da: Bilen kan **køre fast** i den dybe sne.
sentence.en: The car can get stuck in the deep snow.

at køre forbi.explanation: "At køre forbi" means "to drive past". To say you pass a shop in the car: "Vi kører forbi butikken" (We drive past the shop). To say you will visit someone briefly, the phrase means "to swing by": "Jeg kører forbi hos dig i aften" (I will swing by your place tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **køre forbi** og hente dig.
sentence.en: I can swing by and pick you up.

at køre hjem.explanation: "At køre hjem" means "to drive home". To say you go home on foot, use "at gå hjem" (to walk home): "Jeg går hjem" (I am walking home). To say you are already at home, use "hjemme" (at home), not "hjem": "Jeg er hjemme" (I am at home).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **køre hjem**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to drive home.

en kaffeautomat.explanation: "En kaffeautomat" means "a coffee machine". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "en automat" (a vending machine). To talk about the machine you brew coffee with at home, use "en kaffemaskine" (a coffee maker): "Jeg har en kaffemaskine derhjemme" (I have a coffee maker at home).

sentence.da: Jeg kan købe en kop varm kaffe fra en **kaffeautomat** for ti kroner.
sentence.en: I can buy a cup of hot coffee from a vending machine for ten kroner.

en kaffekande.explanation: "En kaffekande" means "a coffee pot". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "en kande" (a pot). The same "kande" is in "en mælkekande" (a milk jug).

sentence.da: Jeg hælder kaffe fra en **kaffekande** i min kop.
sentence.en: I pour coffee from a coffee pot into my cup.

en kaffekop.explanation: "En kaffekop" means "a coffee cup". To name the coffee inside a cup, use "en kop kaffe" (a cup of coffee): "Jeg vil gerne have en kop kaffe" (I would like a cup of coffee).

sentence.da: Min **kaffekop** er tom, og jeg vil have mere.
sentence.en: My coffee cup is empty and I want more.

en kaffemaskine.explanation: "En kaffemaskine" means "a coffee maker". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "en maskine" (a machine). The same "maskine" is in "en vaskemaskine" (a washing machine).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter vand i min **kaffemaskine** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I put water in my coffee maker every morning.

en kaffepause.explanation: "En kaffepause" means "a coffee break". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "en pause" (a break). To say you take a break without naming coffee, use "pause" alone: "Vi holder pause" (We take a break).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **kaffepause** og læser avisen.
sentence.en: I take a coffee break and read the paper.

en kage.explanation: "En kage" means "a cake". To name the kind of cake, put the kind in front of "kage": "en fødselsdagskage" (a birthday cake) and "en chokoladekage" (a chocolate cake).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **kage** til min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: We eat cake for my birthday.

en kagedej.explanation: "En kagedej" means "a cake batter". It is built from "en kage" (a cake) and "en dej" (a dough). To ask to taste the batter: "Må jeg smage kagedejen?" (May I taste the cake batter?)

sentence.da: Jeg hælder **kagedej** i formen og sætter den i ovnen.
sentence.en: I pour cake batter into the pan and put it in the oven.

en kageform.explanation: "En kageform" means "a cake pan". It is built from "kage" (cake) and "en form" (a mold). "Form" also means "a shape". For example, "en kage i form af et hjerte" (a cake in the shape of a heart).

sentence.da: Hun bager en chokoladekage i en **kageform**.
sentence.en: She bakes a chocolate cake in a cake pan.

en kagerulle.explanation: "En kagerulle" means "a rolling pin". It is built from "kage" (cake) and "en rulle" (a roll). To say you flatten dough with it: "Jeg ruller dejen ud med en kagerulle" (I roll out the dough with a rolling pin).

sentence.da: En **kagerulle** er lavet af træ og bruges til dej.
sentence.en: A rolling pin is made of wood and is used for dough.

en kaj.explanation: "En kaj" means "a quay". To say you walk along the water by the boats: "Vi går en tur på kajen" (We take a walk on the quay).

sentence.da: Båden lægger til ved **kaj** nummer to.
sentence.en: The boat docks at quay number two.

en kakerlak.explanation: "En kakerlak" means "a cockroach". To say there are several, use the plural "kakerlakker": "Der er kakerlakker i køkkenet" (There are cockroaches in the kitchen).

sentence.da: Der løb en **kakerlak** hen over køkkengulvet i nat.
sentence.en: A cockroach ran across the kitchen floor last night.

en kalender.explanation: "En kalender" means "a calendar". To say you look up a date, use "i" (in): "Jeg kigger i kalenderen" (I am looking in the calendar).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mødet i min **kalender**.
sentence.en: I write the meeting in my calendar.

en kalkun.explanation: "En kalkun" means "a turkey". When you talk about the meat, leave out "en": "Jeg vil have kalkun på min sandwich" (I want turkey on my sandwich). The country is a different word, "Tyrkiet" (Turkey). For example, "Jeg rejser til Tyrkiet" (I am traveling to Turkey).

sentence.da: Vi steger en stor **kalkun** i ovnen.
sentence.en: We roast a big turkey in the oven.

en kalorie.explanation: "En kalorie" means "a calorie". To say more than one, the plural is "kalorier": "Hvor mange kalorier er der i en pizza?" (How many calories are in a pizza?)

sentence.da: Jeg tæller hver **kalorie** i min mad.
sentence.en: I count every calorie in my food.

en kalv.explanation: "En kalv" means "a calf". To name the meat, use "kalvekød" (veal): "Jeg køber kalvekød til middag" (I am buying veal for dinner).

sentence.da: Koen har fået en lille **kalv**.
sentence.en: The cow has had a little calf.

en kam.explanation: "En kam" means "a comb". To ask to borrow one: "Må jeg låne din kam?" (May I borrow your comb?)

sentence.da: Hun bruger en **kam** i håret.
sentence.en: She uses a comb in her hair.

en kamel.explanation: "En kamel" means "a camel". To say there are several, the plural is "kameler": "Der er mange kameler i ørkenen" (There are many camels in the desert).

sentence.da: En **kamel** kan gå længe uden vand.
sentence.en: A camel can walk for a long time without water.

en kammerat.explanation: "En kammerat" means "a buddy or comrade". To introduce a friend, use it with "min" (my): "Det er min kammerat Peter" (This is my buddy Peter).

sentence.da: Jeg spiller fodbold med en **kammerat** hver lørdag.
sentence.en: I play soccer with a buddy every Saturday.

en kammerjunker.explanation: "En kammerjunker" means "a small Danish cookie". The same word was also an old title at the Danish royal court. To offer one to a guest: "Vil du have en kammerjunker?" (Do you want a small cookie?)

sentence.da: Han dypper sin **kammerjunker** i kaffen, så den bliver blød.
sentence.en: He dips his cookie in the coffee so it gets soft.

en kamp.explanation: "En kamp" means "a match or game". To say a sports game, put the sport in front: "en fodboldkamp" (a soccer game). To say a fight or struggle against something, use "mod" (against): "en kamp mod kræft" (a fight against cancer).

sentence.da: Holdet har en **kamp** mod Brøndby i aften.
sentence.en: The team has a match against Brøndby tonight.

en kampagne.explanation: "En kampagne" means "a campaign". To say a company starts a planned effort, such as in ads: "Firmaet starter en ny kampagne" (The company is starting a new campaign). To say a sale, put "tilbud" (offer) in front: "en tilbudskampagne" (a sale campaign).

sentence.da: Partiet har en stor **kampagne** før valget.
sentence.en: The party has a big campaign before the election.

en kanal.explanation: "En kanal" means "a channel". To ask which TV channel someone watches: "Hvilken kanal ser du?" (Which channel are you watching?) A different meaning is a canal for boats: "en kanal i København" (a canal in Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Jeg skifter til en anden **kanal**.
sentence.en: I switch to another channel.

en kanalrundfart.explanation: "En kanalrundfart" means "a canal tour". It is built from "en kanal" (a canal) and "en rundfart" (a sightseeing trip). To say a TV channel, the word "kanal" works alone as well: "en tv-kanal" (a TV channel).

sentence.da: Vi sejler gennem byen på en **kanalrundfart**.
sentence.en: We sail through the city on a canal tour.

en kandidat.explanation: "En kandidat" means "a candidate". To say a person stands in an election or for a job: "Partiet har en ny kandidat" (The party has a new candidate). A different use is at a university, for someone with a master's degree: "Hun er kandidat fra Aarhus Universitet" (She has a master's degree from Aarhus University).

sentence.da: Hver **kandidat** får ti minutter til at tale om sine planer.
sentence.en: Each candidate gets ten minutes to talk about their plans.

en kanelsnegl.explanation: "En kanelsnegl" means "a cinnamon roll". It is built from "kanel" (cinnamon) and "en snegl" (a snail), because the roll is curled like a snail shell. To order one at a bakery: "Jeg vil gerne have en kanelsnegl" (I would like a cinnamon roll).

sentence.da: Min **kanelsnegl** er sød og smager af kanel.
sentence.en: My cinnamon roll is sweet and tastes of cinnamon.

en kanin.explanation: "En kanin" means "a rabbit". Do not mix it up with "en hare" (a hare), which is a different animal. For example, "Der løber en hare på marken" (A hare is running in the field).

sentence.da: En **kanin** har lange ører og hopper rundt.
sentence.en: A rabbit has long ears and hops around.

en kano.explanation: "En kano" means "a canoe". To say you go canoeing, use "at sejle" (to sail): "Vi sejler i kano" (We go canoeing).

sentence.da: Vi kan leje en **kano** og sejle på søen.
sentence.en: We can rent a canoe and go out on the lake.

en kanon.explanation: "En kanon" means "a cannon". It is built into "en kanonkugle" (a cannonball). In informal Danish, "kanon" also means "great". For example, "Filmen var kanon" (The film was great).

sentence.da: En **kanon** skyder tunge kugler ud af et langt metalrør.
sentence.en: A cannon shoots heavy balls out of a long metal tube.

en kant.explanation: "En kant" means "an edge". To say something is on the edge of a table, use "på kanten af" (on the edge of): "Glasset står på kanten af bordet" (The glass is on the edge of the table).

sentence.da: Pas på, bordet har en skarp **kant**.
sentence.en: Watch out, the table has a sharp edge.

en kantine.explanation: "En kantine" means "a canteen". To say you eat lunch at work or school: "Vi spiser frokost i kantinen" (We eat lunch in the canteen).

sentence.da: Skolen har en **kantine**, og vi køber frokost der.
sentence.en: The school has a canteen, and we buy lunch there.

en kantsten.explanation: "En kantsten" means "a curb". It is built from "en kant" (an edge) and "en sten" (a stone). To say you sit down at the side of the street: "Jeg sætter mig på kantstenen" (I sit down on the curb).

sentence.da: Cyklen kørte ind i en **kantsten** og væltede.
sentence.en: The bike hit a curb and fell.

en kappe.explanation: "En kappe" means "a cloak or robe". To describe a superhero's clothing: "Superhelten har en rød kappe" (The superhero has a red cloak).

sentence.da: Munken har en lang **kappe** med hætte på.
sentence.en: The monk is wearing a long robe with a hood.

en kaptajn.explanation: "En kaptajn" means "a captain". To say who leads a ship: "Kaptajnen styrer skibet" (The captain steers the ship). The leader of a sports team is a different word, "en anfører" (a team leader). For example, "Hun er anfører for holdet" (She is the captain of the team).

sentence.da: Hvert skib har en **kaptajn**, som bestemmer, hvor det sejler.
sentence.en: Every ship has a captain who decides where it sails.

en karakter.explanation: "En karakter" means "a grade or a character". To say what mark you got at school: "Jeg fik en god karakter" (I got a good grade). To describe a person's nature: "Hun har en stærk karakter" (She has a strong character).

sentence.da: Læreren giver mig en **karakter** for opgaven.
sentence.en: The teacher gives me a grade for the assignment.

en karamel.explanation: "En karamel" means "a caramel". To name the sauce, add "sovs" (sauce) to the end: "karamelsovs" (caramel sauce).

sentence.da: En **karamel** er sød og sej og smager af smør.
sentence.en: A caramel is sweet and chewy and tastes of butter.

en karikatur.explanation: "En karikatur" means "a caricature". To say an artist draws a politician with a very big nose: "Tegneren laver en karikatur af politikeren" (The artist makes a caricature of the politician).

sentence.da: Avisen har en **karikatur** af statsministeren med en kæmpestor næse.
sentence.en: The newspaper has a caricature of the prime minister with a giant nose.

en karriere.explanation: "En karriere" means "a career". To say you build one, use "at gøre karriere" (to make a career): "Hun vil gøre karriere i banken" (She wants to make a career in the bank).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne have en **karriere** som læge.
sentence.en: She would like to have a career as a doctor.

en kartoffel.explanation: "En kartoffel" means "a potato". To say how it is cooked, put the cooking word in front of the plural "kartofler": "kogte kartofler" (boiled potatoes) and "stegte kartofler" (fried potatoes).

sentence.da: Jeg skræller en **kartoffel** og koger den.
sentence.en: I peel a potato and boil it.

en karton.explanation: "En karton" means "a carton". To say what is inside, put the contents in front: "en æggekarton" (an egg carton) and "en mælkekarton" (a milk carton).

sentence.da: Mælk og juice kommer ofte i en **karton**.
sentence.en: Milk and juice often come in a carton.

en kasket.explanation: "En kasket" means "a cap". To say a knit hat for cold weather, use "en hue" instead: "Jeg tager en hue på, fordi det er koldt" (I put on a knit hat because it is cold).

sentence.da: Han har en **kasket** med skygge på hovedet.
sentence.en: He has a cap with a visor on his head.

en kasse.explanation: "En kasse" means "a box or checkout". To tell someone where to pay in a store: "Betal ved kassen" (Pay at the checkout). To say a small box, such as for chocolates, use "en æske" instead: "Jeg køber en æske chokolade" (I buy a box of chocolates).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger bøgerne i en stor **kasse**.
sentence.en: I put the books in a big box.

en kassebon.explanation: "En kassebon" means "a register receipt". To tell a customer what to bring when exchanging something: "Husk din kassebon, når du bytter" (Remember your receipt when you exchange something).

related.en: a complaint about a faulty item

sentence.da: Jeg vil bytte varen, men jeg har ikke min **kassebon**.
sentence.en: I want to exchange the item, but I do not have my receipt.

en kassedame.explanation: "En kassedame" means "a cashier". Literally it is "register lady", because "en dame" is a lady. To talk about a man or any person in the job, use "en kassemedarbejder" (a register employee): "Han er kassemedarbejder i et supermarked" (He is a cashier in a supermarket).

sentence.da: Hun arbejder som **kassedame** i en butik.
sentence.en: She works as a cashier in a store.

en kassemedarbejder.explanation: "En kassemedarbejder" means "a cashier". It is built from "kasse" (checkout) and "en medarbejder" (an employee), so it is used for a man or a woman. To say you are applying for the job: "Hun søger job som kassemedarbejder" (She is applying for a job as a cashier).

sentence.da: En **kassemedarbejder** scanner varerne og tager imod betalingen.
sentence.en: A cashier scans the goods and takes the payment.

en kasserolle.explanation: "En kasserolle" means "a saucepan". To say you cook something in it, use "i" (in): "Jeg koger ris i en kasserolle" (I cook rice in a saucepan).

sentence.da: Jeg varmer suppen i en **kasserolle**.
sentence.en: I heat the soup in a saucepan.

en kastanje.explanation: "En kastanje" means "a chestnut". To name the kind you can roast and eat, use "ægte kastanjer" (sweet chestnuts): "Vi ristede ægte kastanjer" (We roasted sweet chestnuts). To name the kind that is not for eating, use "hestekastanjer" (horse chestnuts): "Man kan ikke spise hestekastanjer" (You cannot eat horse chestnuts).

sentence.da: Om efteråret falder en **kastanje** ned fra træet med et bump.
sentence.en: In the fall, a chestnut drops from the tree with a thud.

en kat.explanation: "En kat" means "a cat". To say a cat purrs: "Katten spinder" (The cat purrs). To say you own one, keep "en": "Jeg har en kat" (I have a cat).

sentence.da: Min **kat** siger mjav og drikker mælk.
sentence.en: My cat says meow and drinks milk.

en katastrofe.explanation: "En katastrofe" means "a disaster". To say an event went very badly: "Festen var en katastrofe" (The party was a disaster). To name a flood or storm, put "natur" (nature) in front: "en naturkatastrofe" (a natural disaster).

sentence.da: Oversvømmelsen var en **katastrofe** for byen.
sentence.en: The flood was a disaster for the town.

en katedral.explanation: "En katedral" means "a cathedral". Danish also has the word "en domkirke" (a cathedral), as in "Roskilde Domkirke", where Danish kings and queens are buried.

sentence.da: En **katedral** er større end en almindelig kirke.
sentence.en: A cathedral is bigger than an ordinary church.

en kategori.explanation: "En kategori" means "a category". To say you sort things into groups: "Vi deler ordene op i kategorier" (We divide the words into categories).

sentence.da: Frugt er en **kategori** af mad.
sentence.en: Fruit is a category of food.

en kattebakke.explanation: "En kattebakke" means "a litter box". It is built from "kat" (cat) and "en bakke" (a tray). The word "bakke" also means "a hill", as in "Vi går op ad en bakke" (We walk up a hill).

sentence.da: Katten bruger sin **kattebakke**, når den skal på toilet.
sentence.en: The cat uses its litter box when it needs to use the toilet.

en kaution.explanation: "En kaution" means "a bail payment". To say someone pays so they can wait outside prison, use "at stille kaution" (to put up bail): "Han stillede kaution" (He put up bail).

sentence.da: Hun betalte en **kaution** for at slippe ud af fængslet.
sentence.en: She paid bail to get out of jail.

en kejser.explanation: "En kejser" means "an emperor". A woman in that role is "en kejserinde" (an empress). For example, "Kejserinden bor i paladset" (The empress lives in the palace). The word is also in "et kejsersnit" (a C-section). For another example, "Hun fik et kejsersnit" (She had a C-section).

sentence.da: Romerrigets **kejser** boede i et stort palads i Rom.
sentence.en: The emperor of the Roman Empire lived in a large palace in Rome.

en kemiker.explanation: "En kemiker" means "a chemist". To say a chemist works in a lab: "Kemikeren arbejder i et laboratorium" (The chemist works in a laboratory). Do not use it for the shop worker who gives out medicine; that person is "en apoteker" (a pharmacist): "Jeg køber medicin hos apotekeren" (I buy medicine from the pharmacist).

sentence.da: En **kemiker** blander to væsker for at se, hvad der sker.
sentence.en: A chemist mixes two liquids to see what happens.

en kendelse.explanation: "En kendelse" means "a ruling". To name the paper that lets police search a place, use "en retskendelse" (a court order): "Politiet har fået en retskendelse" (The police have got a court order).

sentence.da: Politiet må have en **kendelse**, før de kan gennemsøge huset.
sentence.en: The police must have a warrant before they can search the house.

en kerne.explanation: "En kerne" means "a core or kernel". To name the seeds inside a fruit, put the fruit in front: "æblekerner" (apple seeds). To name the center of an atom, use "en atomkerne" (an atomic nucleus).

sentence.da: Problemets **kerne** er, at vi ikke har penge nok.
sentence.en: The core of the problem is that we do not have enough money.

en ketsjer.explanation: "En ketsjer" means "a racket". English speakers should note the spelling: it is "ketsjer", not "racket". To say you bring one to a game: "Jeg tager min ketsjer med til tennis" (I bring my racket to tennis).

sentence.da: Man slår til bolden med en **ketsjer** i tennis.
sentence.en: You hit the ball with a racket in tennis.

en kidnapning.explanation: "En kidnapning" means "a kidnapping". The verb is "at kidnappe" (to kidnap). For example, "De kidnappede ham" (They kidnapped him).

sentence.da: Politiet undersøger en **kidnapning** af en rig forretningsmand.
sentence.en: The police are investigating the kidnapping of a rich businessman.

en kikkert.explanation: "En kikkert" means "a pair of binoculars". Danish has one word for it, so no "pair of" is needed. For example, "Jeg har en kikkert" (I have a pair of binoculars).

sentence.da: Med en **kikkert** kan jeg se fuglen langt væk.
sentence.en: With binoculars I can see the bird far away.

en kiks.explanation: "En kiks" means "a biscuit". To talk about crackers with cheese: "kiks og ost" (crackers and cheese). To talk about sweet cookies, use "en småkage" (a cookie): "Hun bager småkager til jul" (She bakes cookies for Christmas).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **kiks** med ost.
sentence.en: I eat a cracker with cheese.

en kilde.explanation: "En kilde" means "a source or spring". To ask where information comes from: "Hvad er din kilde?" (What is your source?) To talk about water coming out of the ground: "en kilde i bjergene" (a spring in the mountains).

sentence.da: Vandet kommer fra en **kilde** i skoven.
sentence.en: The water comes from a spring in the forest.

en killing.explanation: "En killing" means "a kitten". To say there are several, the plural is "killinger": "Der er fire killinger i kurven" (There are four kittens in the basket).

sentence.da: Vores kat har fået en lille **killing**.
sentence.en: Our cat has had a little kitten.

en kilometer.explanation: "En kilometer" means "a kilometer". The plural stays the same. For example, "ti kilometer" (ten kilometers). To give a speed, use "kilometer i timen" (kilometers per hour): "Bilen kører firs kilometer i timen" (The car drives eighty kilometers per hour).

sentence.da: Der er tre **kilometer** til stationen.
sentence.en: It is three kilometers to the station.

en kind.explanation: "En kind" means "a cheek". To talk about both cheeks, the plural is "kinder": "Hendes kinder er røde" (Her cheeks are red).

sentence.da: Hun giver mig et kys på min **kind**.
sentence.en: She gives me a kiss on my cheek.

en kineser.explanation: "En kineser" means "a Chinese person". It comes from "Kina" (China). For things from China, use "kinesisk" (Chinese): "kinesisk mad" (Chinese food).

sentence.da: Min læge er **kineser**, men hun taler godt dansk.
sentence.en: My doctor is Chinese, but she speaks good Danish.

en kiosk.explanation: "En kiosk" means "a kiosk or convenience store". To say you walk to one: "Jeg går ned til kiosken" (I walk down to the kiosk).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en avis i en **kiosk**.
sentence.en: I buy a newspaper at a kiosk.

en kirke.explanation: "En kirke" means "a church". To say you go to church, use "i kirke" (in church) after the verb: "Vi går i kirke i morgen" (We are going to church tomorrow).

sentence.da: Folk beder og synger i en **kirke**.
sentence.en: People pray and sing in a church.

en kirkegård.explanation: "En kirkegård" means "a cemetery". It is built from "en kirke" (a church) and "en gård" (a yard), so it literally means "churchyard". In another word, "gård" means "a farm". For example, "en gård på landet" (a farm in the country).

sentence.da: Der er mange grave på den gamle **kirkegård**.
sentence.en: There are many graves in the old cemetery.

en kirurg.explanation: "En kirurg" means "a surgeon". The subject itself is called "kirurgi" (surgery). To name a surgeon who works on hearts, add the body part in front: "en hjertekirurg" (a heart surgeon).

sentence.da: En **kirurg** kan fjerne blindtarmen, hvis den er betændt.
sentence.en: A surgeon can remove the appendix if it is inflamed.

en kiste.explanation: "En kiste" means "a chest", as in a large box with a lid. In a different meaning, it is a coffin. For example, "Kisten blev båret ud af kirken" (The coffin was carried out of the church).

sentence.da: Skatten lå gemt i en gammel **kiste** under jorden.
sentence.en: The treasure lay hidden in an old chest under the ground.

en kiwi.explanation: "En kiwi" means "a kiwi", as in the fruit. The plural is "kiwier", not "kiwis". For example, "Jeg køber tre kiwier" (I buy three kiwis).

sentence.da: En **kiwi** er grøn indeni og har små sorte kerner.
sentence.en: A kiwi is green inside and has small black seeds.

en kjole.explanation: "En kjole" means "a dress". To name the kind of dress, put a word in front of it: "en festkjole" (a party dress) and "en sommerkjole" (a summer dress).

sentence.da: Hun har en lang **kjole** på til festen.
sentence.en: She is wearing a long dress to the party.

en klage.explanation: "En klage" means "a complaint". The matching verb is "at klage over" (to complain about). To say you want to complain about food, say: "Jeg vil klage over maden" (I want to complain about the food).

sentence.da: Vi sendte en **klage** til firmaet.
sentence.en: We sent a complaint to the company.

en klapvogn.explanation: "En klapvogn" means "a stroller". To say you push it, use "at skubbe" (to push): "Jeg skubber klapvognen" (I push the stroller). For a baby who lies down, use "en barnevogn" (a baby carriage): "Babyen sover i barnevognen" (The baby sleeps in the baby carriage).

sentence.da: Jeg kan folde min **klapvogn** sammen.
sentence.en: I can fold my stroller up.

en klasse.explanation: "En klasse" means "a class", as in a group of pupils. To say which school year a child is in, put a number in front: "Hun går i 2. klasse" (She is in second grade).

sentence.da: Der er tyve børn i min **klasse**.
sentence.en: There are twenty children in my class.

en klassekammerat.explanation: "En klassekammerat" means "a classmate". It is built from "en klasse" (a class) and "en kammerat" (a pal). The word "kammerat" also appears in "en holdkammerat" (a teammate).

sentence.da: Min **klassekammerat** hjælper mig med lektierne.
sentence.en: My classmate helps me with the homework.

en klasselærer.explanation: "En klasselærer" means "a class teacher". It is built from "en klasse" (a class) and "en lærer" (a teacher).

sentence.da: Min **klasselærer** ringede til mine forældre, da jeg var syg.
sentence.en: My class teacher called my parents when I was sick.

en klassificering.explanation: "En klassificering" means "a classification". It comes from the verb "at klassificere" (to classify).

sentence.da: Biologer arbejder med **klassificering** af levende ting i arter.
sentence.en: Biologists work with the classification of living things into species.

en klassiker.explanation: "En klassiker" means "a classic". To say a dish has always been on a restaurant's menu, say: "en klassiker på menuen" (a classic on the menu). For classical music, use the adjective "klassisk" (classical): "Jeg lytter til klassisk musik" (I listen to classical music).

sentence.da: Den gamle film er blevet en **klassiker**, som alle har set.
sentence.en: The old movie has become a classic that everyone has seen.

en klat.explanation: "En klat" means "a dollop or blob". To name what the blob is made of, put the material straight after "klat", with no word for "of": "en klat maling" (a blob of paint).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **klat** smør på brødet.
sentence.en: I put a dollop of butter on the bread.

en klejne.explanation: "En klejne" means "a Christmas cruller". It is a traditional Danish Christmas pastry: a twisted strip of dough fried in fat.

sentence.da: Til jul spiser vi en sprød **klejne** med kaffe.
sentence.en: At Christmas we eat a crisp cruller with coffee.

en klemme.explanation: "En klemme" means "a clothespin or clip". In a different meaning, to say someone is stuck in a tight spot, use "at sidde i klemme" (to be in a bind): "Jeg sidder i klemme" (I am in a bind).

sentence.da: Hver sok hænger på snoren med en **klemme**.
sentence.en: Each sock hangs on the line with a clothespin.

en klient.explanation: "En klient" means "a client". In a shop or café, the word for a person who buys is "en kunde" (a customer). For example, "Kunden betaler ved kassen" (The customer pays at the register).

sentence.da: Advokaten møder sin **klient** i morgen klokken ti.
sentence.en: The lawyer meets her client tomorrow at ten.

en klinik.explanation: "En klinik" means "a clinic". To say someone is in a hospital, use "et sygehus" or "et hospital" (both mean a hospital): "Min mor ligger på sygehuset" (My mother is in the hospital).

sentence.da: Jeg ser en læge på en **klinik**.
sentence.en: I see a doctor at a clinic.

en klipning.explanation: "En klipning" means "a haircut". To say you are getting one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg skal have en klipning i morgen" (I am getting a haircut tomorrow). For the style itself, use "en frisure" (a hairstyle): "Hun har en ny frisure" (She has a new hairstyle).

sentence.da: Jeg har booket en **klipning**, fordi mit hår er blevet for langt.
sentence.en: I booked a haircut because my hair has gotten too long.

en klippe.explanation: "En klippe" means "a cliff or rock". Do not mix it up with the verb "at klippe" (to cut). For example, "Jeg klipper papir" (I cut paper).

sentence.da: Vi sad på en stor **klippe** og så på havet.
sentence.en: We sat on a big rock and looked at the sea.

en klit.explanation: "En klit" means "a sand dune". Denmark has tall sand dunes along the west coast of Jutland.

sentence.da: Vinden har blæst sandet op til en høj **klit**.
sentence.en: The wind has blown the sand up into a tall dune.

en klo.explanation: "En klo" means "a claw". To say someone falls into another person's power, use "at falde i kløerne på" (to fall into the clutches of): "Musen faldt i kløerne på katten" (The mouse fell into the clutches of the cat).

sentence.da: En ørn har en skarp **klo** på hver tå.
sentence.en: An eagle has a sharp claw on each toe.

en klode.explanation: "En klode" means "a planet". The form "kloden" means "the Earth", as in "rundt om kloden" (around the globe). For a planet such as Mars, the ordinary word is "en planet": "Mars er en planet" (Mars is a planet).

sentence.da: Der bor otte milliarder mennesker på vores **klode**.
sentence.en: Eight billion people live on our planet.

en klods.explanation: "En klods" means "a block". The word "klods" is also the end of "legoklodser" (Lego bricks).

sentence.da: Hun sætter en **klods** oven på tårnet.
sentence.en: She puts a block on top of the tower.

en klokke.explanation: "En klokke" means "a bell". When you ask what time it is, you use the form "klokken" (the bell): "Hvad er klokken?" (What time is it?)

sentence.da: Jeg hører en **klokke** ringe i kirken.
sentence.en: I hear a bell ring in the church.

en klovn.explanation: "En klovn" means "a clown". In a different meaning, it describes a person who acts foolishly. For example, "Stop med at være en klovn" (Stop being a clown).

sentence.da: Den sjove **klovn** har en stor rød næse.
sentence.en: The funny clown has a big red nose.

en klub.explanation: "En klub" means "a club", as in a group of people. To say you join one, use "at melde sig ind i" (to join): "Jeg melder mig ind i en klub" (I join a club).

sentence.da: Jeg spiller skak i en **klub** hver torsdag.
sentence.en: I play chess in a club every Thursday.

en klud.explanation: "En klud" means "a cloth or rag". For drying plates, use "et viskestykke" (a dish towel): "Jeg tørrer tallerkenen med et viskestykke" (I dry the plate with a dish towel).

sentence.da: Tag en **klud**, og tør vandet op!
sentence.en: Take a cloth and wipe up the water!

en klump.explanation: "En klump" means "a lump". To say a smooth mix has lumps in it, use the plural: "Der er klumper i saucen" (There are lumps in the sauce).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **klump** smør og smelter den i panden.
sentence.en: I take a lump of butter and melt it in the pan.

en kløver.explanation: "En kløver" means "a clover". To name a clover with four leaves, use "en firkløver" (a four-leaf clover). In a card game, "kløver" is also the suit of clubs. For example, "Hvem har kløver es?" (Who has the ace of clubs?)

sentence.da: Der vokser hvid **kløver** i plænen hele sommeren.
sentence.en: White clover grows in the lawn all summer.

en knage.explanation: "En knage" means "a coat hook". To tell someone to hang a coat up, say: "Hæng jakken på knagen" (Hang the jacket on the hook).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger min jakke på en **knage** i gangen.
sentence.en: I hang my jacket on a coat hook in the hallway.

en knallert.explanation: "En knallert" means "a moped". In Denmark, a moped with a top speed of 45 km/h is called "en knallert 45".

sentence.da: En **knallert** er langsommere end en motorcykel.
sentence.en: A moped is slower than a motorcycle.

en knap.explanation: "En knap" means "a button". In a different meaning, the word "knap" without "en" means "barely". For example, "Jeg har knap nok tid" (I barely have time).

sentence.da: Der mangler en **knap** på min jakke.
sentence.en: A button is missing on my jacket.

en knibe.explanation: "I knibe" means "in a fix". To say someone gets into trouble, use "komme i knibe" (to get into trouble): "Han kommer i knibe, hvis han glemmer det" (He will be in trouble if he forgets it). To say you help someone out, use "hjælpe en ud af knibe" (to help someone out of a fix): "Jeg hjælper dig ud af knibe" (I will help you out of a fix).

forms.en: to help someone out of a fix

sentence.da: Jeg er i **knibe**, fordi jeg har mistet min nøgle.
sentence.en: I am in a fix because I have lost my key.

en kniv.explanation: "En kniv" means "a knife". To say you eat with cutlery, put "kniv" before "gaffel" (fork): "Jeg spiser med kniv og gaffel" (I eat with a knife and fork).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer brød med en **kniv**.
sentence.en: I cut bread with a knife.

en knivspids.explanation: "En knivspids" means "a pinch", as in a small amount. It is built from "en kniv" (a knife) and "en spids" (a tip). To name what the pinch is made of, put the ingredient straight after it, with no word for "of": "en knivspids kanel" (a pinch of cinnamon).

sentence.da: Tilsæt en **knivspids** salt til suppen.
sentence.en: Add a pinch of salt to the soup.

en knogle.explanation: "En knogle" means "a bone". To say someone has broken a bone, use "at brække" (to break): "Han har brækket en knogle i foden" (He has broken a bone in his foot).

sentence.da: Røntgen viser, om en **knogle** er brækket.
sentence.en: The X-ray shows whether a bone is broken.

en knop.explanation: "En knop" means "a bud". Do not mix it up with "en knap" (a button). For example, "Der mangler en knap på jakken" (A button is missing on the jacket).

sentence.da: Træet har en lille **knop**, som åbner sig i morgen.
sentence.en: The tree has a small bud that opens tomorrow.

en knude.explanation: "En knude" means "a knot". To say your hair is tangled, use: "en knude i håret" (a knot in the hair). In a different meaning, a tight spot in a muscle is also a knot. For example, "en knude i nakken" (a knot in the neck).

sentence.da: Der er en **knude** på rebet.
sentence.en: There is a knot in the rope.

en knægt.explanation: "En knægt" means "a lad or kid". For a boy, the ordinary word is "en dreng" (a boy): "Drengen leger i haven" (The boy plays in the garden).

sentence.da: Han er kun otte, men han er en stærk **knægt**.
sentence.en: He is only eight, but he is a strong lad.

en ko.explanation: "En ko" means "a cow". The plural is "køer", not "koer". For example, "Der står tre køer på marken" (Three cows stand in the field).

sentence.da: En **ko** spiser græs på marken.
sentence.en: A cow eats grass in the field.

en koalition.explanation: "En koalition" means "a coalition". To say groups join together in one, use "at danne" (to form): "De tre grupper dannede en koalition" (The three groups formed a coalition).

sentence.da: Den nye regering er en **koalition** mellem tre partier.
sentence.en: The new government is a coalition between three parties.

en kobling.explanation: "En kobling" means "a clutch", as in the pedal of a car. In a different meaning, it is the coupling that joins two train cars. For example, "en kobling mellem to togvogne" (a coupling between two train cars).

sentence.da: Bilen har en **kobling**, så man kan skifte gear.
sentence.en: The car has a clutch so that you can change gears.

en kode.explanation: "En kode" means "a code". In a different meaning, it is computer code. For example, "Han skriver kode" (He writes code).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge en **kode** for at åbne døren.
sentence.en: You need a code to open the door.

en kofanger.explanation: "En kofanger" means "a bumper". It is built from "en ko" (a cow) and "at fange" (to catch), so it literally means "cow catcher".

sentence.da: Der er en bule i min **kofanger**.
sentence.en: There is a dent in my bumper.

en kogeplade.explanation: "En kogeplade" means "a hotplate". It is built from "at koge" (to boil, to cook) and "en plade" (a plate).

sentence.da: Jeg stiller den varme gryde på en **kogeplade**.
sentence.en: I put the hot pot on a hotplate.

en kogle.explanation: "En kogle" means "a pine cone". To name the tree, put it in front: "en grankogle" (a spruce cone).

sentence.da: Hver **kogle** på træet gemmer små frø mellem skællene.
sentence.en: Each cone on the tree hides small seeds between its scales.

en kogning.explanation: "En kogning" means "a boiling". It comes from the verb "at koge" (to boil). To tell someone to bring a pot to a boil, say: "Bring det i kog" (Bring it to a boil).

sentence.da: Efter **kogning** skal pastaen køle lidt af.
sentence.en: After boiling, the pasta needs to cool a little.

en kok.explanation: "En kok" means "a chef". Do not mix it up with "at koge" (to boil). For example, "Jeg koger æg" (I boil eggs).

sentence.da: Min bror er **kok** på en restaurant.
sentence.en: My brother is a chef at a restaurant.

en kokkeelev.explanation: "En kokkeelev" means "a chef apprentice". It is built from "en kok" (a cook) and "en elev" (a pupil). The word "elev" also appears in "en skoleelev" (a school pupil).

sentence.da: Som **kokkeelev** lærer jeg at lave mad på en restaurant.
sentence.en: As a chef apprentice, I learn to cook at a restaurant.

en koldskål.explanation: "En koldskål" means "a cold buttermilk dessert". It is a Danish dish eaten with small crisp cookies called "kammerjunkere".

sentence.da: Efter en varm dag smager en **koldskål** dejligt.
sentence.en: After a hot day, a koldskål tastes lovely.

en kollega.explanation: "En kollega" means "a colleague". The plural is "kolleger", not "kollegaer". For example, "Mine kolleger spiser frokost sammen" (My colleagues eat lunch together).

sentence.da: Min **kollega** og jeg arbejder sammen på kontoret.
sentence.en: My colleague and I work together in the office.

en kolonihave.explanation: "En kolonihave" means "an allotment garden". In Denmark, it is a small rented plot with a little house on it, in an area with many other plots. The word is built from "en koloni" (a colony) and "en have" (a garden).

sentence.da: Min familie har en **kolonihave**, hvor vi dyrker grøntsager.
sentence.en: My family has an allotment garden where we grow vegetables.

en kombination.explanation: "En kombination" means "a combination". In a different meaning, it is the set of numbers that opens a lock. For example, "Jeg glemte kombinationen" (I forgot the combination).

sentence.da: Pasta og ost er en god **kombination**.
sentence.en: Pasta and cheese are a good combination.

en komedie.explanation: "En komedie" means "a comedy". For a sad story, use "en tragedie" (a tragedy): "Filmen er en tragedie" (The film is a tragedy).

sentence.da: Vi griner hele aftenen, fordi filmen er en **komedie**.
sentence.en: We laugh all evening because the film is a comedy.

en komet.explanation: "En komet" means "a comet". To name the most famous comet, say "Halleys komet" (Halley's comet).

sentence.da: Vi kan se en **komet** med en lang hale på himlen.
sentence.en: We can see a comet with a long tail in the sky.

en komiker.explanation: "En komiker" means "a comedian". To name a comedian who performs stand-up, use "en stand-up-komiker" (a stand-up comedian).

sentence.da: En **komiker** står på scenen og får publikum til at le.
sentence.en: A comedian stands on the stage and makes the audience laugh.

en kommando.explanation: "En kommando" means "a command". To say something happens when someone gives the order, use "på kommando" (on command): "Soldaterne marcherer på kommando" (The soldiers march on command). In a different meaning, it is a line you type in a computer. For example, "Skriv kommandoen i terminalen" (Type the command in the terminal).

sentence.da: Hunden sætter sig på **kommando**.
sentence.en: The dog sits on command.

en kommandør.explanation: "En kommandør" means "a commander". It comes from "en kommando" (a command).

sentence.da: En **kommandør** leder en stor styrke af soldater og skibe.
sentence.en: A commander leads a large force of soldiers and ships.

en kommentar.explanation: "En kommentar" means "a comment". The action is "at kommentere" (to comment). To say you comment on a video, say: "Jeg kommenterer videoen" (I comment on the video).

sentence.da: Jeg læste hver **kommentar** under opslaget.
sentence.en: I read every comment under the post.

en kommentator.explanation: "En kommentator" means "a commentator". It comes from the verb "at kommentere" (to comment).

sentence.da: En **kommentator** forklarer, hvad der sker i kampen.
sentence.en: A commentator explains what is happening in the match.

en kommissær.explanation: "En kommissær" means "a commissioner". To name a member of the European Commission, use "en EU-kommissær" (an EU commissioner).

sentence.da: En **kommissær** i EU har ansvar for et bestemt område.
sentence.en: A commissioner in the EU is responsible for a certain area.

en kommode.explanation: "En kommode" means "a chest of drawers". Danish spells it with a "k" where English "commode" has a "c".

sentence.da: Mit tøj ligger i en hvid **kommode**.
sentence.en: My clothes are in a white chest of drawers.

en kommune.explanation: "En kommune" means "a municipality". Denmark is divided into 98 municipalities.

sentence.da: Vores **kommune** bygger en ny skole.
sentence.en: Our municipality is building a new school.

en komponist.explanation: "En komponist" means "a composer". The ending "-ist" marks a person in other words. For example, "en pianist" (a pianist) and "en turist" (a tourist).

sentence.da: En **komponist** skriver noder, som andre senere spiller.
sentence.en: A composer writes sheet music that others play later.

en koncentration.explanation: "En koncentration" means "a concentration". In a different meaning, it is how much of a substance is in a mix. For example, "koncentrationen af salt i vandet" (the concentration of salt in the water).

sentence.da: Det kræver **koncentration** at læse i et støjende rum.
sentence.en: It takes concentration to read in a noisy room.

en koncert.explanation: "En koncert" means "a concert". To say you go to a concert, leave out "en": "Vi går til koncert i aften" (We are going to a concert tonight).

sentence.da: Bandet spiller mange sange på en **koncert**.
sentence.en: The band plays many songs at a concert.

en kondicykel.explanation: "En kondicykel" means "an exercise bike". The start "kondi" is short for "kondition" (fitness). For example, "Jeg har god kondition" (I have good stamina).

sentence.da: Når det regner, træner jeg på min **kondicykel** i stuen.
sentence.en: When it rains, I work out on my exercise bike in the living room.

en kondolence.explanation: "En kondolence" means "a condolence". The verb is "at kondolere" (to offer condolences): "Jeg kondolerer" (My condolences).

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig min dybfølte **kondolence** efter dødsfaldet.
