sentence.en: I am sending you my deepest condolences after the death.

en kone.explanation: "En kone" means "a wife". For a woman in general, use "en kvinde" (a woman): "Kvinden står ved bussen" (The woman stands at the bus).

sentence.da: Han giftede sig med sin **kone** i 2010.
sentence.en: He married his wife in 2010.

en konfirmation.explanation: "En konfirmation" means "a confirmation". In Denmark, young people are confirmed around age 14, and the party after it is called "en konfirmationsfest" (a confirmation party).

sentence.da: Min lillebror har **konfirmation** i foråret.
sentence.en: My little brother has his confirmation in the spring.

en konflikt.explanation: "En konflikt" means "a conflict". To say people solve one, use "at løse" (to solve): "De løste konflikten" (They solved the conflict).

sentence.da: Der er opstået en **konflikt** mellem de to naboer om hækken.
sentence.en: A conflict has arisen between the two neighbors over the hedge.

en konge.explanation: "En konge" means "a king". Denmark's official name is "Kongeriget Danmark" (the Kingdom of Denmark).

sentence.da: En **konge** styrer et land.
sentence.en: A king rules a country.

en konklusion.explanation: "En konklusion" means "a conclusion". In a different meaning, it is the last part of a report. For example, "Læs konklusionen først" (Read the conclusion first).

sentence.da: Efter mange tests kom forskerne til en **konklusion**.
sentence.en: After many tests, the researchers came to a conclusion.

en konkurrence.explanation: "En konkurrence" means "a competition". The verb is "at konkurrere" (to compete). To say someone won it, use "at vinde" (to win): "Hun vandt konkurrencen" (She won the competition).

sentence.da: Man kan vinde en pris i en **konkurrence**.
sentence.en: You can win a prize in a competition.

en konkurrent.explanation: "En konkurrent" means "a competitor". It comes from the verb "at konkurrere" (to compete).

sentence.da: Vores **konkurrent** sælger de samme varer til lavere priser.
sentence.en: Our competitor sells the same goods at lower prices.

en konsekvens.explanation: "En konsekvens" means "a consequence". To say something will have consequences, use "at få konsekvenser" (to have consequences): "Det vil få konsekvenser" (There will be consequences). Do not mix it up with the adjective "konsekvent" (consistent). For example, "Hun er altid konsekvent" (She is always consistent).

sentence.da: Hans træthed er en **konsekvens** af for lidt søvn.
sentence.en: His tiredness is a consequence of too little sleep.

en konsistens.explanation: "En konsistens" means "a texture". Do not use it for English "consistency" in the sense of doing the same thing each time. For that, use "konsekvent" (consistent): "Hun er altid konsekvent" (She is always consistent).

sentence.da: Budding har en blød og glat **konsistens**.
sentence.en: Pudding has a soft and smooth texture.

en konsonant.explanation: "En konsonant" means "a consonant". To name the other kind of letter, use "en vokal" (a vowel): "E er en vokal" (E is a vowel).

sentence.da: I ordet bog er b en **konsonant** og o en vokal.
sentence.en: In the word bog, b is a consonant and o is a vowel.

en konsulent.explanation: "En konsulent" means "a consultant". It comes from the verb "at konsultere" (to consult).

sentence.da: Firmaet har hyret en **konsulent** til at give råd om økonomien.
sentence.en: The company has hired a consultant to give advice about the finances.

en kontakt.explanation: "En kontakt" means "a contact or a switch". When you talk about a person you know who can help you, it means "a contact": "Jeg har en kontakt i banken" (I have a contact at the bank). When you talk about the thing you press to turn on a light, it means "a switch": "Kontakten er ved døren" (The switch is by the door).

sentence.da: Jeg har stadig **kontakt** med min gamle ven.
sentence.en: I still have contact with my old friend.

en kontaktlinse.explanation: "En kontaktlinse" means "a contact lens". It is built from "en kontakt" (a contact) and "en linse" (a lens).

sentence.da: Hun har en **kontaktlinse** i hvert øje i stedet for briller.
sentence.en: She has a contact lens in each eye instead of glasses.

en kontaktløs betaling.explanation: "En kontaktløs betaling" means "a contactless payment". The ending "-løs" means "without". For example, "kontaktløs" is "without contact", and "håbløs" (hopeless) uses the same ending.

sentence.da: Ved **kontaktløs betaling** holder du bare telefonen hen til terminalen.
sentence.en: With contactless payment you just hold the phone up to the terminal.

en kontaktperson.explanation: "En kontaktperson" means "a contact person". To say a man or a woman is the contact person, the word stays the same: "Han er vores kontaktperson" (He is our contact person) and "Hun er vores kontaktperson" (She is our contact person).

sentence.da: Min **kontaktperson** på skolen hedder Anne.
sentence.en: My contact person at the school is called Anne.

en kontekst.explanation: "En kontekst" means "a context". To say words are used in the wrong setting, use "taget ud af kontekst" (taken out of context): "Ordene er taget ud af kontekst" (The words are taken out of context).

sentence.da: Uden **kontekst** kan man ikke se, hvad ordet betyder.
sentence.en: Without context you cannot tell what the word means.

en konto.explanation: "En konto" means "an account", as in an account at a bank. To say you open one, use "at oprette" (to open, to set up): "Jeg vil gerne oprette en konto" (I would like to open an account).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter penge ind på min **konto**.
sentence.en: I put money into my account.

en kontorassistent.explanation: "En kontorassistent" means "an office assistant". It is built from "et kontor" (an office) and "en assistent" (an assistant).

sentence.da: Vi har ansat en ny **kontorassistent** til at hjælpe på kontoret.
sentence.en: We have hired a new office assistant to help in the office.

en kontorplads.explanation: "En kontorplads" means "a workspace". For a whole room, use "et kontor" (an office): "Jeg har mit eget kontor" (I have my own office).

sentence.da: Min nye **kontorplads** er ved vinduet, så jeg har dagslys.
sentence.en: My new workspace is by the window, so I have daylight.

en kontorstol.explanation: "En kontorstol" means "an office chair". It is built from "et kontor" (an office) and "en stol" (a chair). The word "stol" also appears in "en spisestol" (a dining chair).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder på en god **kontorstol** hele dagen.
sentence.en: I sit on a good office chair all day.

en kontrakt.explanation: "En kontrakt" means "a contract". For an agreement that is only spoken, use "en aftale" (an agreement): "Vi har en mundtlig aftale" (We have a spoken agreement).

sentence.da: Før du skriver under, skal du læse hele din **kontrakt**.
sentence.en: Before you sign, you must read your whole contract.

en kontrast.explanation: "En kontrast" means "a contrast". To compare two things, use "i kontrast til" (in contrast to): "I kontrast til sommeren er vinteren mørk" (In contrast to the summer, the winter is dark).

sentence.da: Der er stor **kontrast** mellem den lyse væg og det sorte gulv.
sentence.en: There is a big contrast between the light wall and the black floor.

en kontrol.explanation: "En kontrol" means "a check or control". When the police or a border guard stops you to look at your papers, it means "a check": "Der er kontrol ved grænsen" (There is a check at the border). When you talk about power over something, it means "control": "Han har kontrol over bilen" (He has control of the car).

sentence.da: Politiet laver en **kontrol** på vejen.
sentence.en: The police are doing a check on the road.

en kontrolafgift.explanation: "En kontrolafgift" means "a penalty fare". It is built from "en kontrol" (a check) and "en afgift" (a fee). To say you must pay it, say: "Jeg skal betale en kontrolafgift" (I have to pay a penalty fare).

sentence.da: Uden billet får du en **kontrolafgift**.
sentence.en: Without a ticket, you get a penalty fare.

en koordinat.explanation: "En koordinat" means "a coordinate". To ask for the place of something, use the plural: "Send mig koordinaterne til stedet" (Send me the coordinates for the place).

sentence.da: Breddegraden er en **koordinat** på et kort.
sentence.en: Latitude is a coordinate on a map.

en kop.explanation: "En kop" means "a cup". To name what is in the cup, put the drink straight after "kop", with no word for "of": "en kop te" (a cup of tea).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **kop** kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like a cup of coffee.

en kopi.explanation: "En kopi" means "a copy". To ask someone to make one, use "at lave" (to make): "Kan du lave en kopi af nøglen?" (Can you make a copy of the key?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge en **kopi** af dit pas.
sentence.en: I need a copy of your passport.

en kopimaskine.explanation: "En kopimaskine" means "a copier". It is built from "en kopi" (a copy) and "en maskine" (a machine). The word "maskine" also appears in "en vaskemaskine" (a washing machine).

sentence.da: Kan du lave ti kopier på vores **kopimaskine**?
sentence.en: Can you make ten copies on our copier?

en korporal.explanation: "En korporal" means "a corporal". To use the rank with a name, put it before the name: "korporal Hansen" (Corporal Hansen).

sentence.da: En **korporal** er over en menig og under en sergent.
sentence.en: A corporal is above a private and below a sergeant.

en kosmetolog.explanation: "En kosmetolog" means "a beautician". For someone who cuts hair, use "en frisør" (a hairdresser): "Frisøren klipper mit hår" (The hairdresser cuts my hair).

sentence.da: Min **kosmetolog** giver mig en ansigtsbehandling hver anden måned.
sentence.en: My beautician gives me a facial every other month.

en kost.explanation: "En kost" means "a broom". In a different meaning, the word "kost" without "en" means "diet". For example, "sund kost" (a healthy diet). For cleaning a floor with electricity, use "en støvsuger" (a vacuum cleaner): "Støvsugeren står i skabet" (The vacuum cleaner is in the cupboard).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **kost** og fejer køkkenet.
sentence.en: I take a broom and sweep the kitchen.

en kostald.explanation: "En kostald" means "a cowshed". It is built from "ko" (cow) and "en stald" (a shed for farm animals). To say the sheep are in their shed, use "stald" alone: "Fårene er i stalden" (The sheep are in the shed).

sentence.da: Køerne sover i en stor, varm **kostald**.
sentence.en: The cows sleep in a big, warm cowshed.

en krabbe.explanation: "En krabbe" means "a crab". When you talk about crab as food, leave out "en": "Vi spiser krabbe" (We eat crab).

sentence.da: En lille **krabbe** går sidelæns over sandet.
sentence.en: A small crab walks sideways over the sand.

en kraft.explanation: "En kraft" means "a force or power". To say how strong the wind is, use it for physical force: "Vinden har stor kraft" (The wind has great force). To say someone did something with all their strength, use the phrase "af alle kræfter" (with all one's might): "Han skubbede af alle kræfter" (He pushed with all his might). To talk about power over other people, as in politics, use "magt" (power): "Politikerne har magt" (The politicians have power).

sentence.da: Vinden havde så stor **kraft**, at den væltede træet.
sentence.en: The wind had so much force that it knocked over the tree.

en krage.explanation: "En krage" means "a crow". One kind of crow is "en gråkrage" (a hooded crow), built from "grå" (gray) and "krage". For example, "Gråkragen sidder på taget" (The hooded crow sits on the roof).

sentence.da: En **krage** leder ofte efter mad på marker og i byer.
sentence.en: A crow often looks for food in fields and in towns.

en krampe.explanation: "En krampe" means "a cramp". To say a muscle cramps, use the phrase "at få krampe i" (to get a cramp in): "Jeg får krampe i foden" (I get a cramp in my foot).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **krampe** i læggen, da jeg svømmede.
sentence.en: I got a cramp in my calf when I was swimming.

en kran.explanation: "En kran" means "a crane". When you talk about water in a sink, "en kran" also means "a faucet": "Luk for kranen" (Turn off the faucet).

sentence.da: Den høje **kran** løfter tunge ting.
sentence.en: The tall crane lifts heavy things.

en krans.explanation: "En krans" means "a wreath". In Denmark, a wreath with four candles is lit on the four Sundays before Christmas. It is called "en adventskrans" (an Advent wreath), built from "advent" (Advent) and "krans". For example, "Vi tænder adventskransen" (We light the Advent wreath).

sentence.da: På døren hænger der en **krans** af grene til jul.
sentence.en: On the door hangs a wreath of branches for Christmas.

en kransekage.explanation: "En kransekage" means "a marzipan ring cake". It is a Danish tower of stacked rings, served at New Year and at weddings. It is built from "en krans" (a wreath) and "en kage" (a cake).

sentence.da: Vi spiser en **kransekage** med marcipan til nytår.
sentence.en: We eat a marzipan ring cake at New Year.

en krave.explanation: "En krave" means "a collar". To talk about the collar on a dog, use "et halsbånd" (a dog collar): "Hunden har et rødt halsbånd" (The dog has a red collar).

sentence.da: Jakken har en høj **krave**, som holder halsen varm.
sentence.en: The jacket has a high collar that keeps the neck warm.

en krig.explanation: "En krig" means "a war". To say countries are fighting each other, use the phrase "i krig" (at war), with no "en": "Landene er i krig" (The countries are at war). The opposite is "fred" (peace). For example, "Vi vil have fred" (We want peace).

sentence.da: Den lange **krig** sluttede i foråret.
sentence.en: The long war ended in the spring.

en krimi.explanation: "En krimi" means "a crime novel or show". It is short for "kriminalroman" (crime novel). To say you watch one on TV, use the same word: "Vi ser en ny krimi i aften" (We are watching a new crime show tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en spændende **krimi** i aften.
sentence.en: I am reading an exciting crime novel tonight.

en kriminalassistent.explanation: "En kriminalassistent" means "a detective sergeant". It is built from "kriminal" (criminal) and "en assistent" (an assistant).

sentence.da: En **kriminalassistent** efterforsker sagen og taler med vidnerne.
sentence.en: A detective sergeant investigates the case and talks to the witnesses.

en kriminalbetjent.explanation: "En kriminalbetjent" means "a detective". It is built from "kriminal" (criminal) and "en betjent" (an officer).

sentence.da: En **kriminalbetjent** undersøger tyverier og andre forbrydelser.
sentence.en: A detective investigates thefts and other offenses.

en krise.explanation: "En krise" means "a crisis". To say someone is going through a crisis, use the phrase "i krise" (in crisis), with no "en": "Hun er i krise" (She is in crisis).

sentence.da: Landet er midt i en **krise**, og mange mister deres job.
sentence.en: The country is in the middle of a crisis, and many are losing their jobs.

en kritiker.explanation: "En kritiker" means "a critic". It comes from "kritik" (criticism). To talk about a person who speaks against a plan, add "af" (of): "Kritikerne af planen er uenige" (The critics of the plan disagree).

sentence.da: En **kritiker** skriver i avisen om nye film og bøger.
sentence.en: A critic writes in the newspaper about new films and books.

en kro.explanation: "En kro" means "an inn". It is a Danish kind of inn where you can eat a meal and also rent a room. To suggest a meal there, say: "Skal vi spise på kroen?" (Shall we eat at the inn?)

sentence.da: Vi spiser og sover på en lille **kro** på landet.
sentence.en: We eat and sleep at a small inn in the countryside.

en krog.explanation: "En krog" means "a hook or corner". When you talk about a small cozy corner of a room, use "en hyggelig krog" (a cozy corner): "Jeg sidder i en hyggelig krog" (I am sitting in a cozy corner).

sentence.da: Hæng jakken på en **krog** ved døren.
sentence.en: Hang the jacket on a hook by the door.

en krokodille.explanation: "En krokodille" means "a crocodile". To say someone cries without meaning it, use "krokodilletårer" (crocodile tears): "Han græd krokodilletårer" (He cried crocodile tears).

sentence.da: En **krokodille** har skarpe tænder.
sentence.en: A crocodile has sharp teeth.

en krone.explanation: "En krone" means "a crown (currency)". After a number, you say "kroner": "tyve kroner" (twenty crowns). In prices, it is written "kr.". For example, "Det koster 20 kr." (It costs 20 crowns). It also means the crown on a king's head. For example, "Kongen har en krone på hovedet" (The king has a crown on his head).

sentence.da: En **krone** er hundrede øre.
sentence.en: A krone is a hundred øre.

en kronik.explanation: "En kronik" means "an op-ed". To ask whether someone has read today's op-ed, say: "Har du læst kronikken i dag?" (Have you read the op-ed today?)

sentence.da: Forskeren skrev en **kronik** i avisen om skolens fremtid.
sentence.en: The researcher wrote an op-ed in the paper about the future of schools.

en kronisk sygdom.explanation: "En kronisk sygdom" means "a chronic illness". It is built from the adjective "kronisk" (chronic) and "en sygdom" (an illness). The adjective is also used for other things: "Han er kronisk træt" (He is chronically tired).

sentence.da: Mange lever et normalt liv med en **kronisk sygdom**.
sentence.en: Many people live a normal life with a chronic illness.

en krop.explanation: "En krop" means "a body". To say a body part hurts, Danish says "the" where English says "my": "Jeg har ondt i maven" (My stomach hurts). To say your whole body aches, say: "Jeg har ondt i kroppen" (My whole body aches).

sentence.da: Min **krop** er meget træt i dag.
sentence.en: My body is very tired today.

en krukke.explanation: "En krukke" means "a jar". It is also part of "en blomsterkrukke" (a flowerpot), built from "en blomst" (a flower) and "krukke". For example, "Planten står i en blomsterkrukke" (The plant is in a flowerpot).

sentence.da: Der står en **krukke** honning i skabet.
sentence.en: There is a jar of honey in the cupboard.

en krydderurt.explanation: "En krydderurt" means "an herb". It is built from "krydder" (spice) and "en urt" (a plant). "Et krydderi" (a spice) is a different word. For example, "Peber er et krydderi" (Pepper is a spice).

sentence.da: Basilikum er en **krydderurt** i mange italienske retter.
sentence.en: Basil is an herb in many Italian dishes.

en krydsogtværs.explanation: "En krydsogtværs" means "a crossword". It comes from the phrase "kryds og tværs" (literally, "cross and across"). To say people ran in every direction, use that phrase: "De løb kryds og tværs" (They ran in all directions).

sentence.da: Hver søndag løser jeg en **krydsogtværs** i avisen.
sentence.en: Every Sunday I solve a crossword in the newspaper.

en krykke.explanation: "En krykke" means "a crutch". To say someone walks with crutches, use "gå på krykker" (walk on crutches): "Han går på krykker" (He walks on crutches). To talk about both crutches together, say "et par krykker" (a pair of crutches): "Jeg skal have et par krykker" (I need to get a pair of crutches).

sentence.da: Med et brækket ben støtter man sig til en **krykke**.
sentence.en: With a broken leg you lean on a crutch.

en kuffert.explanation: "En kuffert" means "a suitcase". To say you pack for a trip, use "at pakke" (to pack): "Jeg pakker kufferten i aften" (I am packing the suitcase tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg har tøj i min **kuffert**.
sentence.en: I have clothes in my suitcase.

en kugle.explanation: "En kugle" means "a ball or bullet". To talk about a ball used in sports, such as a football, use "en bold" (a ball): "Han sparker til bolden" (He kicks the ball).

sentence.da: Barnet leger med en **kugle** på gulvet.
sentence.en: The child plays with a marble on the floor.

en kuglepen.explanation: "En kuglepen" means "a ballpoint pen". It is built from "en kugle" (a ball) and "en pen" (a pen), named after the tiny ball in the tip. To ask to borrow a ballpoint pen, say: "Må jeg låne din kuglepen?" (May I borrow your ballpoint pen?)

sentence.da: Jeg skriver et brev med en blå **kuglepen**.
sentence.en: I write a letter with a blue ballpoint pen.

en kujon.explanation: "En kujon" means "a coward". It is an insult, so it is rude to say it to someone. To shout it at a person, you say: "Din kujon!" (You coward!)

sentence.da: Han kaldte mig en **kujon**, fordi jeg ikke turde springe.
sentence.en: He called me a coward because I did not dare to jump.

en kuldebølge.explanation: "En kuldebølge" means "a cold spell". It is built from "kulde" (cold) and "en bølge" (a wave). To say the weather report warns about one, use "at varsle" (to warn): "Vejrudsigten varsler en kuldebølge" (The forecast warns of a cold spell).

sentence.da: Under en **kuldebølge** er det flere dage i træk under frysepunktet.
sentence.en: During a cold spell it is below freezing for several days in a row.

en kuling.explanation: "En kuling" means "a gale". To say a gale blows today, say: "Der er kuling i dag" (There is a gale today). A stronger wind is "en storm" (a storm). For example, "Der er storm i dag" (There is a storm today).

sentence.da: Vejrudsigten melder **kuling** ved kysten i aften.
sentence.en: The forecast says there will be a gale on the coast tonight.

en kultur.explanation: "En kultur" means "a culture". When you talk about art, music and theater, you also use it: "Der er meget kultur i København" (There is a lot of culture in Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Jeg vil lære mere om dansk **kultur**.
sentence.en: I want to learn more about Danish culture.

en kulturforskel.explanation: "En kulturforskel" means "a cultural difference". It is built from "kultur" (culture) and "en forskel" (a difference). To say two countries differ, use "mellem" (between): "Der er en stor kulturforskel mellem Danmark og Italien" (There is a big cultural difference between Denmark and Italy).

sentence.da: Det er en **kulturforskel**, at danskere spiser aftensmad så tidligt.
sentence.en: It is a cultural difference that Danes eat dinner so early.

en kunde.explanation: "En kunde" means "a customer". It is also the first part of "kundeservice" (customer service). For example, "Ring til kundeservice" (Call customer service).

sentence.da: En **kunde** betaler for varerne i butikken.
sentence.en: A customer pays for the goods in the store.

en kunsthistoriker.explanation: "En kunsthistoriker" means "an art historian". It is built from "kunst" (art) and "en historiker" (a historian). To say you study the subject, use "at studere" (to study): "Hun studerer kunsthistorie" (She studies art history).

sentence.da: På museet fortæller en **kunsthistoriker** om malerierne.
sentence.en: At the museum an art historian tells about the paintings.

en kunstner.explanation: "En kunstner" means "an artist". It is built from "kunst" (art). To talk about a musician or singer, you also use it: "Han er en kendt kunstner, der synger" (He is a famous artist who sings).

sentence.da: Den danske **kunstner** maler store billeder.
sentence.en: The Danish artist paints big pictures.

en kunstudstilling.explanation: "En kunstudstilling" means "an art exhibition". It is built from "kunst" (art) and "en udstilling" (an exhibition). The opening evening is called "en fernisering" (an opening reception). For example, "Vi er inviteret til ferniseringen" (We are invited to the opening).

sentence.da: På en **kunstudstilling** kan man se malerier og skulpturer.
sentence.en: At an art exhibition you can see paintings and sculptures.

en kur.explanation: "En kur" means "a cure". To talk about a fixed program of eating less to lose weight, use "en slankekur" (a weight-loss diet): "Hun er på slankekur" (She is on a diet).

sentence.da: Lægerne leder efter en **kur** mod sygdommen.
sentence.en: The doctors are looking for a cure for the disease.

en kurs.explanation: "En kurs" means "a course (direction) or exchange rate". To say a pilot changes direction, use "at skifte kurs" (to change course): "Piloten skifter kurs" (The pilot changes course). To talk about money, use it for the exchange rate: "Dollarens kurs er høj i dag" (The dollar's exchange rate is high today). A class you attend is "et kursus" (a course). For example, "Jeg tager et kursus i dansk" (I am taking a course in Danish).

sentence.da: Skibet holder **kurs** mod nord, selvom bølgerne er store.
sentence.en: The ship keeps its course north, even though the waves are big.

en kurv.explanation: "En kurv" means "a basket". To say you put your goods in the basket at a shop, use "en indkøbskurv" (a shopping basket): "Læg varerne i indkøbskurven" (Put the goods in the shopping basket).

sentence.da: Æblerne ligger i en **kurv** med hank.
sentence.en: The apples are in a basket with a handle.

en kusine.explanation: "En kusine" means "a female cousin". Danish has a separate word for a male cousin, "en fætter". For example, "Min fætter bor i Aarhus" (My male cousin lives in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Min **kusine** er datter af min tante.
sentence.en: My cousin is my aunt's daughter.

en kuvert.explanation: "En kuvert" means "an envelope". To tell someone to write the address on an envelope, say: "Skriv adressen på kuverten" (Write the address on the envelope).

sentence.da: Brevet ligger i en hvid **kuvert** med frimærke.
sentence.en: The letter is in a white envelope with a stamp.

en kvadratmeter.explanation: "En kvadratmeter" means "a square meter". It is built from "kvadrat" (square) and "en meter" (a meter). To say how big a home is, say: "Lejligheden er firs kvadratmeter" (The apartment is eighty square meters).

sentence.da: Vores stue er cirka tyve **kvadratmeter**.
sentence.en: Our living room is about twenty square meters.

en kvalifikation.explanation: "En kvalifikation" means "a qualification". To say someone is suited for a job, use "de rette kvalifikationer" (the right qualifications): "Hun har de rette kvalifikationer til jobbet" (She has the right qualifications for the job).

sentence.da: Hendes vigtigste **kvalifikation** er ti års erfaring som sygeplejerske.
sentence.en: Her most important qualification is ten years of experience as a nurse.

en kvalitet.explanation: "En kvalitet" means "a quality". When you talk about how good something is, use it: "Det er god kvalitet" (It is good quality). When you talk about a good trait in a person, it also works: "Ærlighed er en kvalitet" (Honesty is a quality).

sentence.da: Jeg vil hellere købe én ting af høj **kvalitet**.
sentence.en: I would rather buy one thing of high quality.

en kvinde.explanation: "En kvinde" means "a woman". To talk about a girl, use "en pige" (a girl): "Pigen går i skole" (The girl goes to school).

sentence.da: En mand og en **kvinde** går forbi.
sentence.en: A man and a woman walk past.

en kvittering.explanation: "En kvittering" means "a receipt". To ask for a receipt in a shop, say: "Må jeg få en kvittering?" (May I have a receipt?)

sentence.da: Jeg betalte i butikken og fik en **kvittering**.
sentence.en: I paid in the store and got a receipt.

en kyst.explanation: "En kyst" means "a coast". To say you live close to the sea, use "ved kysten" (by the coast): "Vi bor ved kysten" (We live by the coast).

sentence.da: Det er en lang **kyst** med mange strande.
sentence.en: It is a long coast with many beaches.

en kystby.explanation: "En kystby" means "a coastal town". It is built from "en kyst" (a coast) and "en by" (a town). The word "by" is also in "en landsby" (a village). For example, "Han bor i en landsby" (He lives in a village).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en lille **kystby**, og havet er tæt på.
sentence.en: We live in a small coastal town, and the sea is close.

en kæbe.explanation: "En kæbe" means "a jaw". To say a jaw is broken, use "at brække" (to break): "Han har brækket kæben" (He has broken his jaw).

sentence.da: Tænderne sidder fast i din **kæbe**.
sentence.en: The teeth are fixed in your jaw.

en kæde.explanation: "En kæde" means "a chain". When you talk about shops owned by one company, it also means a group of shops: "en kæde af butikker" (a chain of stores).

sentence.da: Min cykel har en rusten **kæde**.
sentence.en: My bike has a rusty chain.

en kælder.explanation: "En kælder" means "a basement". To say where you keep things, use "i kælderen" (in the basement): "Vi opbevarer cyklerne i kælderen" (We keep the bikes in the basement).

sentence.da: Under huset ligger en mørk **kælder**.
sentence.en: Under the house there is a dark basement.

en kæledyrsforsikring.explanation: "En kæledyrsforsikring" means "a pet insurance policy". It is built from "et kæledyr" (a pet), the joining "s" and "en forsikring" (an insurance policy). To say you took out a policy, use "at tegne" (to take out): "Vi har tegnet en kæledyrsforsikring til hunden" (We have taken out pet insurance for the dog).

sentence.da: Hundens operation var dyr, men vores **kæledyrsforsikring** betalte det meste.
sentence.en: The dog's operation was expensive, but our pet insurance paid most of it.

en kæmpe.explanation: "En kæmpe" means "a giant". When you put "kæmpe" before another word, it means "huge": "en kæmpe fejl" (a huge mistake).

sentence.da: I eventyret møder drengen en **kæmpe**.
sentence.en: In the fairy tale, the boy meets a giant.

en kæreste.explanation: "En kæreste" means "a partner (romantic)". It is the same word for a man and a woman. To ask someone about their love life, say: "Har du en kæreste?" (Do you have a boyfriend or girlfriend?)

sentence.da: Jeg bor sammen med min **kæreste**.
sentence.en: I live together with my partner.

en kø.explanation: "En kø" means "a queue". To say you wait in line, use "at stå i kø" (to stand in a queue), with no "en": "Vi står i kø til biografen" (We are standing in line for the cinema). When you talk about cars, it also means a traffic jam: "Der er kø på motorvejen" (There is a traffic jam on the highway).

sentence.da: Der er en lang **kø** ved kassen.
sentence.en: There is a long line at the checkout.

en københavner.explanation: "En københavner" means "a Copenhagener". It is built from "København" (Copenhagen). Other cities have a similar word, such as "en aarhusianer" (a person from Aarhus). For example, "Min ven er aarhusianer" (My friend is from Aarhus).

sentence.da: Som **københavner** tager jeg ofte cyklen på arbejde.
sentence.en: As a Copenhagener I often take the bike to work.

en købmand.explanation: "En købmand" means "a grocer or shopkeeper". It is built from "at købe" (to buy) and "en mand" (a man). To say you shop at the local grocer's, say: "Jeg handler hos købmanden" (I shop at the grocer's).

sentence.da: Vores **købmand** har altid friske grøntsager.
sentence.en: Our grocer always has fresh vegetables.

en kødbolle.explanation: "En kødbolle" means "a meatball". It is built from "kød" (meat) and "en bolle" (a ball). In the Danish dish "boller i karry" (meatballs in curry), the meatballs are called just "boller". For example, "Vi spiser boller i karry til middag" (We eat meatballs in curry for dinner).

sentence.da: Rul det hakkede kød til en **kødbolle** og steg den.
sentence.en: Roll the minced meat into a meatball and fry it.

en kødspiser.explanation: "En kødspiser" means "a meat eater". The opposite is "en vegetar" (a vegetarian). For example, "Han er vegetar" (He is a vegetarian).

sentence.da: Min bror er **kødspiser**, men min søster spiser kun grøntsager.
sentence.en: My brother is a meat eater, but my sister only eats vegetables.

en køjeseng.explanation: "En køjeseng" means "a bunk bed". It is built from "en køje" (a bunk) and "en seng" (a bed). To say which bunk you sleep in, say: "Jeg sover i den øverste køje" (I sleep in the top bunk).

sentence.da: To børn sover over hinanden i en **køjeseng**.
sentence.en: Two children sleep above each other in a bunk bed.

en køkkenchef.explanation: "En køkkenchef" means "a head chef". It is built from "køkken" (kitchen) and "en chef" (a boss). To say what someone does for a living, say: "Hun er køkkenchef på en restaurant" (She is head chef at a restaurant).

sentence.da: Som **køkkenchef** planlægger hun menuen og leder alle kokkene.
sentence.en: As head chef she plans the menu and leads all the cooks.

en køkkenhave.explanation: "En køkkenhave" means "a vegetable garden", literally "a kitchen garden". It is built from "køkken" (kitchen) and "en have" (a garden). A garden for flowers only is "en prydhave" (an ornamental garden). For example, "Der er blomster og buske i prydhaven" (There are flowers and bushes in the ornamental garden).

sentence.da: I vores **køkkenhave** gror der gulerødder, kartofler og salat.
sentence.en: In our vegetable garden, carrots, potatoes and lettuce grow.

en køkkenrulle.explanation: "En køkkenrulle" means "a roll of paper towels". It is built from "køkken" (kitchen) and "en rulle" (a roll). To ask someone to pass it, say: "Kan du række mig køkkenrullen?" (Can you hand me the paper towels?)

sentence.da: Jeg har spildt mælk og skal bruge en **køkkenrulle**.
sentence.en: I have spilled milk and need a roll of paper towels.

en køkkenvægt.explanation: "En køkkenvægt" means "a kitchen scale". It is built from "køkken" (kitchen) and "en vægt" (a scale). The word "vægt" also means "weight". For example, "Jeg vil gerne tabe vægt" (I want to lose weight).

sentence.da: Jeg vejer melet på en **køkkenvægt**.
sentence.en: I weigh the flour on a kitchen scale.

en kørelærer.explanation: "En kørelærer" means "a driving instructor". It is built from "at køre" (to drive) and "en lærer" (a teacher). The verb "at køre" is also used for going by vehicle: "Jeg kører med bussen" (I go by bus).

sentence.da: Min **kørelærer** sidder ved siden af mig i bilen.
sentence.en: My driving instructor sits next to me in the car.

en køreplan.explanation: "En køreplan" means "a timetable". It is built from "at køre" (to drive) and "en plan" (a plan). To find out when a bus leaves, use "at tjekke" (to check): "Jeg tjekker køreplanen for bussen" (I check the timetable for the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg kigger i en **køreplan**, fordi jeg tager toget.
sentence.en: I look in a timetable because I am taking the train.

en køreprøve.explanation: "En køreprøve" means "a driving test". It is built from "at køre" (to drive) and "en prøve" (a test). To say you sit the test, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager køreprøven i næste uge" (I am taking the driving test next week).

sentence.da: Hun bestod sin **køreprøve** i går.
sentence.en: She passed her driving test yesterday.

en køreskole.explanation: "En køreskole" means "a driving school". It is built from "at køre" (to drive) and "en skole" (a school). To say you have a lesson, use "en køretime" (a driving lesson): "Jeg har en køretime i morgen" (I have a driving lesson tomorrow).

sentence.da: Min søster går på **køreskole** og lærer at køre.
sentence.en: My sister goes to driving school and learns to drive.

en kørestol.explanation: "En kørestol" means "a wheelchair". To say someone uses a wheelchair, use "sidde i kørestol" (sit in a wheelchair), with no "en": "Han sidder i kørestol" (He uses a wheelchair).

sentence.da: Hun kan ikke gå, så hun bruger en **kørestol**.
sentence.en: She cannot walk, so she uses a wheelchair.

en kørsel.explanation: "En kørsel" means "a drive or trip". On a road sign, it names the act of driving. For example, "Kørsel forbudt" (No driving).

sentence.da: En **kørsel** til lufthavnen tager en time.
sentence.en: A drive to the airport takes an hour.

et kaffebord.explanation: "Et kaffebord" means "a coffee-and-cake gathering". In Denmark, it is held after a christening, a confirmation or a funeral. The table in a living room is a different thing, "et sofabord" (a living-room table). For example, "Kopperne står på sofabordet" (The cups are on the living-room table).

sentence.da: Efter dåben var der **kaffebord** med lagkage til alle gæsterne.
sentence.en: After the christening, there was coffee and cake for all the guests.

et kaffefilter.explanation: "Et kaffefilter" means "a coffee filter". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "et filter" (a filter). The plural is "kaffefiltre" (coffee filters), not "kaffefiltere", because the "e" before "r" drops out.

sentence.da: Kaffemaskinen virker ikke uden et **kaffefilter**.
sentence.en: The coffee machine does not work without a coffee filter.

et kalenderlys.explanation: "Et kalenderlys" means "an Advent calendar candle". In Denmark, it is a candle marked with the numbers 1 to 24, which you burn down one number each day in December. It is built from "en kalender" (a calendar) and "et lys" (a candle).

sentence.da: Et **kalenderlys** hjælper børnene med at tælle dagene til jul.
sentence.en: An Advent calendar candle helps the children count the days until Christmas.

et kamera.explanation: "Et kamera" means "a camera". To say you take a photo with it, say: "Jeg tager et foto med kameraet" (I take a photo with the camera).

sentence.da: Min telefon har et rigtig godt **kamera**.
sentence.en: My phone has a really good camera.

et kapitel.explanation: "Et kapitel" means "a chapter". When you talk about a period of someone's life, it also works: "Det var et vigtigt kapitel i hans liv" (It was an important chapter in his life).

sentence.da: Jeg læser et **kapitel** hver aften.
sentence.en: I read a chapter every evening.

et karaktergennemsnit.explanation: "Et karaktergennemsnit" means "a grade point average". It is built from "en karakter" (a grade) and "et gennemsnit" (an average). In Denmark, grades run from -3 to 12. To ask about someone's average, say: "Hvad er dit karaktergennemsnit?" (What is your grade point average?)

sentence.da: Med et højt **karaktergennemsnit** kan man komme ind på de fleste uddannelser.
sentence.en: With a high grade point average, you can get into most programs.

et kartotekskort.explanation: "Et kartotekskort" means "an index card". It is built from "et kartotek" (a card file) and "et kort" (a card).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver ordet på et **kartotekskort** og lærer det udenad.
sentence.en: I write the word on an index card and learn it by heart.

et kasino.explanation: "Et kasino" means "a casino". To say someone gambles there, use "at spille" (to play): "Han spiller roulette på kasinoet" (He plays roulette at the casino).

sentence.da: Vi spiller kort med penge på et **kasino**.
sentence.en: We play cards for money at a casino.

et katalog.explanation: "Et katalog" means "a catalog". To say you buy from it, use "at bestille" (to order): "Jeg bestiller tøj fra kataloget" (I order clothes from the catalog).

sentence.da: Jeg bladrer i et **katalog** og finder en ny jakke.
sentence.en: I flip through a catalog and find a new jacket.

et kemikalie.explanation: "Et kemikalie" means "a chemical". To warn someone, say: "Pas på kemikalier!" (Be careful with chemicals!)

sentence.da: Man skal bruge handsker, når man arbejder med et **kemikalie**.
sentence.en: You must wear gloves when you work with a chemical.

et kendetegn.explanation: "Et kendetegn" means "a characteristic". It is built from "at kende" (to know) and "et tegn" (a sign), so it is literally "a sign to know something by".

sentence.da: Sorte og hvide striber er et **kendetegn** ved zebraen.
sentence.en: Black and white stripes are a characteristic of the zebra.

et kilo.explanation: "Et kilo" means "a kilo". It is short for "et kilogram" (a kilogram). To ask for an amount in a shop, say: "To kilo kartofler, tak" (Two kilos of potatoes, please).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have et **kilo** æbler.
sentence.en: I would like a kilo of apples.

et kirsebær.explanation: "Et kirsebær" means "a cherry". The word ends in "bær" (berry), as in "et jordbær" (a strawberry).

sentence.da: Jeg putter et **kirsebær** på kagen.
sentence.en: I put a cherry on the cake.

et klasseværelse.explanation: "Et klasseværelse" means "a classroom". It is built from "en klasse" (a class) and "et værelse" (a room). When you talk about a school year, "klasse" also works: "Hun går i tredje klasse" (She is in third grade).

sentence.da: Eleverne sidder i et lyst **klasseværelse**.
sentence.en: The students sit in a bright classroom.

et klaver.explanation: "Et klaver" means "a piano". To say you take piano lessons, use "gå til" (go to): "Jeg går til klaver om tirsdagen" (I take piano lessons on Tuesdays).

sentence.da: Hun spiller **klaver** hjemme.
sentence.en: She plays the piano at home.

et klima.explanation: "Et klima" means "a climate". Do not mix it up with "et vejr" (weather), which is about one day. For example, "Det er dårligt vejr i dag" (The weather is bad today).

sentence.da: Danmark har et mildt **klima**, men det regner meget.
sentence.en: Denmark has a mild climate, but it rains a lot.

et klimaks.explanation: "Et klimaks" means "a climax". To say the tension in a story reaches its peak, use "at nå" (to reach): "Spændingen når sit klimaks i sidste kapitel" (The tension reaches its climax in the last chapter).

sentence.da: Bogens **klimaks** er, når helten endelig møder skurken.
sentence.en: The climax of the book is when the hero finally meets the villain.

et klip.explanation: "Et klip" means "a cut or clip". When you talk about one quick snip with scissors, use it: "Ét klip, og snoren var skåret over" (One snip, and the string was cut).

sentence.da: Jeg sendte min veninde et sjovt **klip** fra filmen.
sentence.en: I sent my friend a funny clip from the movie.

et klippekort.explanation: "Et klippekort" means "a punch card". It is built from "et klip" (a punch) and "et kort" (a card). To say how many rides are left, count the punches: "Klippekortet har tre klip tilbage" (The punch card has three punches left).

sentence.da: Jeg har et **klippekort** med ti ture.
sentence.en: I have a punch card with ten rides.

et kloster.explanation: "Et kloster" means "a monastery or convent". Danish uses the same word whether men or women live there. To say someone became a nun or monk, use "gå i kloster" (enter a monastery or convent): "Hun gik i kloster som ung" (She entered a convent when she was young).

sentence.da: Munke og nonner bor sammen i et **kloster** og beder hver dag.
sentence.en: Monks and nuns live together in a monastery and pray every day.

et klædeskab.explanation: "Et klædeskab" means "a wardrobe". It is built from "klæder" (clothes) and "et skab" (a cupboard). The part "skab" is also in "et køleskab" (a fridge). For example, "Mælken står i køleskabet" (The milk is in the fridge).

sentence.da: Tøjet hænger i et **klædeskab** i soveværelset.
sentence.en: The clothes hang in a wardrobe in the bedroom.

et knep.explanation: "Et knep" means "a trick". A magic trick is a different thing, "et tryllenummer" (a magic act). For example, "Børnene elsker tryllenummeret" (The children love the magic act).

sentence.da: Hun kender et **knep** til at få tøjet tørt hurtigere.
sentence.en: She knows a trick for getting the clothes dry faster.

et knus.explanation: "Et knus" means "a hug". To end a message to a friend, you can write: "Knus fra Maria" (Hugs from Maria).

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig et stort **knus**.
sentence.en: I am sending you a big hug.

et knæ.explanation: "Et knæ" means "a knee". Unlike in English, you pronounce the "k": say "k-næ". To tell someone to bend their knees, say: "Bøj knæene!" (Bend your knees!)

sentence.da: Hun faldt og slog sit **knæ**.
sentence.en: She fell and hurt her knee.

et kodeord.explanation: "Et kodeord" means "a password". It is built from "en kode" (a code) and "et ord" (a word), so it is literally "a code word". To ask for it, say: "Hvad er dit kodeord?" (What is your password?)

sentence.da: Jeg har glemt mit **kodeord**.
sentence.en: I have forgotten my password.

et kollegieværelse.explanation: "Et kollegieværelse" means "a dorm room". It is built from "et kollegium" (a student dormitory) and "et værelse" (a room). To say you rent one, use "at leje" (to rent): "Jeg lejer et kollegieværelse i Aarhus" (I rent a dorm room in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Mit **kollegieværelse** er lille, og der står kun en seng og et skrivebord.
sentence.en: My dorm room is small, and there is only a bed and a desk.

et kollegium.explanation: "Et kollegium" means "a student dormitory". To say someone lives in a dorm, use "på" (at) and leave out "et": "Han bor på kollegium" (He lives in a dorm).

sentence.da: Jeg flytter ind på **kollegium** i september.
sentence.en: I am moving into a dorm in September.

et kolon.explanation: "Et kolon" means "a colon", as in the punctuation mark. To introduce a list, you write the colon before the list: "Jeg skal bruge tre ting: mel, æg og sukker" (I need three things: flour, eggs and sugar).

sentence.da: Et **kolon** består af to prikker over hinanden.
sentence.en: A colon is made of two dots on top of each other.

en koma.explanation: "En koma" means "a coma". To say someone is in a coma, use "i koma" (in a coma): "Hun lå i koma i to uger" (She was in a coma for two weeks). Spell it with one "m".

sentence.da: Lægerne lagde patienten i kunstigt **koma**, så kroppen kunne hele.
sentence.en: The doctors put the patient in an induced coma so the body could heal.

et komfur.explanation: "Et komfur" means "a stove". To say where a pot sits, use "på komfuret" (on the stove): "Suppen står på komfuret" (The soup is on the stove).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad på et gammelt **komfur**.
sentence.en: We cook on an old stove.

et komma.explanation: "Et komma" means "a comma". In numbers, Danish uses a comma where English uses a point. For example, "tre komma fem" (three point five), written "3,5". Spell it with two "m".

sentence.da: Der skal stå et **komma** foran ordet men.
sentence.en: There must be a comma in front of the word men (but).

et kommunalvalg.explanation: "Et kommunalvalg" means "a local election". It is built from "en kommune" (a municipality) and "et valg" (an election). To say you vote in it, use "at stemme" (to vote) with "ved": "Jeg stemmer ved kommunalvalget" (I vote in the local election).

sentence.da: Hvert fjerde år er der et **kommunalvalg**, hvor man vælger byrådet.
sentence.en: Every four years there is a local election, where you choose the city council.

et kompagni.explanation: "Et kompagni" means "a company (military or business)". As a business, it appears in the name "Det Østasiatiske Kompagni" (the East Asiatic Company).

sentence.da: Et **kompagni** består af flere mindre grupper af soldater.
sentence.en: A company consists of several smaller groups of soldiers.

et kompas.explanation: "Et kompas" means "a compass". For a person's sense of right and wrong, use "et moralsk kompas" (a moral compass): "Hun har et stærkt moralsk kompas" (She has a strong moral compass).

sentence.da: Vi bruger et **kompas** til at finde vej.
sentence.en: We use a compass to find our way.

et kompliment.explanation: "Et kompliment" means "a compliment". To answer a compliment, say "Tak for komplimentet" (Thanks for the compliment).

sentence.da: Hun gav mig et **kompliment** for min kjole.
sentence.en: She gave me a compliment on my dress.

et kompromis.explanation: "Et kompromis" means "a compromise". To say people reach one, use "at indgå et kompromis" (to reach a compromise): "De indgik et kompromis" (They reached a compromise).

sentence.da: Vi kunne ikke blive enige, så vi fandt et **kompromis**.
sentence.en: We could not agree, so we found a compromise.

et koncerthus.explanation: "Et koncerthus" means "a concert hall". It is built from "en koncert" (a concert) and "et hus" (a house).

sentence.da: Orkestret spiller for tusind tilhørere i et stort **koncerthus**.
sentence.en: The orchestra plays for a thousand listeners in a big concert hall.

et konditori.explanation: "Et konditori" means "a pastry shop or café". It comes from "en konditor" (a pastry chef).

sentence.da: På et **konditori** kan man sidde ned og spise kage med kaffe.
sentence.en: At a pastry shop, you can sit down and eat cake with coffee.

et kondom.explanation: "Et kondom" means "a condom". To say you use one, Danish leaves out "et": "at bruge kondom" (to use a condom).

sentence.da: Et **kondom** beskytter både mod graviditet og mod seksuelt overførte sygdomme.
sentence.en: A condom protects against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases.

et kongehus.explanation: "Et kongehus" means "a royal family". It is built from "en konge" (a king) and "et hus" (a house), so it is literally a "king house".

sentence.da: Et **kongehus** er den familie, som har en konge eller en dronning.
sentence.en: A royal family is the family that has a king or a queen.

et kongerige.explanation: "Et kongerige" means "a kingdom". It is built from "en konge" (a king) and "et rige" (a realm). Denmark's official name is "Kongeriget Danmark" (the Kingdom of Denmark), which also includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

sentence.da: Danmark er et **kongerige**, fordi landet har en konge.
sentence.en: Denmark is a kingdom because the country has a king.

et kongresmedlem.explanation: "Et kongresmedlem" means "a member of Congress". It is built from "kongres" (congress) and "et medlem" (a member). For a member of the Danish parliament, use "et folketingsmedlem": "Hun er folketingsmedlem" (She is a member of the Danish parliament).

sentence.da: Et **kongresmedlem** stemmer om nye love i Washington.
sentence.en: A member of Congress votes on new laws in Washington.

et konsulat.explanation: "Et konsulat" means "a consulate". It comes from "en konsul" (a consul). To say where you are going, use "på konsulatet" (at the consulate): "Jeg skal på konsulatet i morgen" (I am going to the consulate tomorrow).

sentence.da: Hvis du mister dit pas i udlandet, kan du få hjælp på et **konsulat**.
sentence.en: If you lose your passport abroad, you can get help at a consulate.

et kontantbeløb.explanation: "Et kontantbeløb" means "a cash amount". It is built from "kontant" (in cash) and "et beløb" (an amount). To say you pay in cash, use "kontant": "Jeg betaler kontant" (I pay in cash).

sentence.da: Kontrakten kræver et **kontantbeløb** på ti tusind kroner.
sentence.en: The contract requires a cash amount of ten thousand kroner.

et kontinent.explanation: "Et kontinent" means "a continent". Some continent names are spelled differently from English. For example, "Europa" (Europe) and "Asien" (Asia).

sentence.da: Afrika er et **kontinent** med mange lande.
sentence.en: Africa is a continent with many countries.

et kontor.explanation: "Et kontor" means "an office". To say where you are, use "på kontoret" (at the office): "Jeg er på kontoret" (I am at the office).

sentence.da: Hun arbejder ved en computer på et **kontor**.
sentence.en: She works at a computer in an office.

et kontorhus.explanation: "Et kontorhus" means "an office building". It is built from "et kontor" (an office) and "et hus" (a house).

sentence.da: Mange firmaer har kontorer i et **kontorhus**.
sentence.en: Many companies have offices in an office building.

et kor.explanation: "Et kor" means "a choir". To say people do something all together, use "i kor" (in chorus): "De råbte i kor" (They shouted in chorus).

sentence.da: Hun synger i et **kor** hver tirsdag.
sentence.en: She sings in a choir every Tuesday.

et kors.explanation: "Et kors" means "a cross". For the X you tick on a form, use "et kryds" (an X mark): "Sæt et kryds her" (Put an X here).

sentence.da: Danmarks flag har et hvidt **kors** på rød baggrund.
sentence.en: The flag of Denmark has a white cross on a red background.

et kort.explanation: "Et kort" means "a map or a card". When you mean a map, say "et kort over Danmark" (a map of Denmark). When you mean a card, say "et kreditkort" (a credit card). The same spelling is also the adjective "short". For example, "en kort tur" (a short trip).

sentence.da: Jeg kigger på et **kort** over byen.
sentence.en: I look at a map of the town.

et kortspil.explanation: "Et kortspil" means "a card game". It is built from "et kort" (a card) and "et spil" (a game). To say you play cards, use "at spille kort" (to play cards): "Vi spiller kort i aften" (We are playing cards tonight).

sentence.da: Poker er et populært **kortspil**.
sentence.en: Poker is a popular card game.

et kosttilskud.explanation: "Et kosttilskud" means "a dietary supplement". It is built from "kost" (diet) and "et tilskud" (an addition).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **kosttilskud** med D-vitamin hver dag.
sentence.en: I take a supplement with vitamin D every day.

et kostume.explanation: "Et kostume" means "a costume". To name a party where everyone dresses up, use "en kostumefest" (a costume party): "Vi holder kostumefest" (We are having a costume party).

sentence.da: Børn har **kostume** på til fastelavn.
sentence.en: Children wear costumes at carnival.

et kostumebal.explanation: "Et kostumebal" means "a costume party". It is built from "et kostume" (a costume) and "et bal" (a dance party). To say you go to one, use "til" (to): "Jeg skal til kostumebal i aften" (I am going to a costume party tonight).

sentence.da: Til et **kostumebal** er alle klædt ud som figurer eller dyr.
sentence.en: At a costume party, everyone is dressed up as characters or animals.

et kraftværk.explanation: "Et kraftværk" means "a power plant". It is built from "kraft" (power) and "et værk" (a works). "Værk" also ends "et stålværk" (a steel mill).

sentence.da: Et **kraftværk** laver strøm til tusindvis af hjem.
sentence.en: A power plant makes electricity for thousands of homes.

et kram.explanation: "Et kram" means "a hug". It is the noun for the verb "at kramme" (to hug). To say a mother hugs her son, use the verb: "Hun krammer sin søn" (She hugs her son).

sentence.da: Min datter gav mig et stort **kram**.
sentence.en: My daughter gave me a big hug.

et kranie.explanation: "Et kranie" means "a skull". For the skull as a warning symbol, use "et dødningehoved" (a death's head): "Piratflaget har et dødningehoved" (The pirate flag has a skull).

sentence.da: Hjernen er beskyttet af et hårdt **kranie**.
sentence.en: The brain is protected by a hard skull.

et krat.explanation: "Et krat" means "a thicket". For one single plant, use "en busk" (a bush) instead: "Der står en busk ved døren" (There is a bush by the door).

sentence.da: Rådyret gemmer sig i et tæt **krat** ved søen.
sentence.en: The roe deer hides in a dense thicket by the lake.

et krav.explanation: "Et krav" means "a requirement". When you insist on something, it also means "a demand": "Hun stiller høje krav" (She makes high demands). The verb that goes with it is "at stille" (to put), as in "at stille krav" (to make demands).

sentence.da: Der er et **krav** om, at man skal være atten år.
sentence.en: There is a requirement that you must be eighteen years old.

et kreditkort.explanation: "Et kreditkort" means "a credit card". It is built from "kredit" (credit) and "et kort" (a card). The part "kort" also means "a map", as in "et landkort" (a map of a country).

sentence.da: Kan jeg betale med **kreditkort** her?
sentence.en: Can I pay with a credit card here?

et kredsløb.explanation: "Et kredsløb" means "a circuit or circulation". It is built from "en kreds" (a circle) and "et løb" (a run). For the path of a satellite around the Earth, it also means "an orbit": "en satellits kredsløb" (a satellite's orbit).

sentence.da: Blodets **kredsløb** går rundt i hele kroppen.
sentence.en: The circulation of the blood goes around the whole body.

et kriterium.explanation: "Et kriterium" means "a criterion". To say you meet one, use "at opfylde" (to fulfill): "Han opfylder kriteriet" (He meets the criterion).

sentence.da: Prisen er det vigtigste **kriterium**, når vi vælger en bil.
sentence.en: The price is the most important criterion when we choose a car.

et kronblad.explanation: "Et kronblad" means "a petal". It is built from "en krone" (a crown) and "et blad" (a leaf).

related.en: a sepal (green leaf under the petals)

sentence.da: Hvert **kronblad** på solsikken er gult.
sentence.en: Each petal on the sunflower is yellow.

et krus.explanation: "Et krus" means "a mug". For a normal cup, use "en kop" (a cup) instead: "En kop te, tak" (A cup of tea, please).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker min kaffe af et stort **krus**.
sentence.en: I drink my coffee from a big mug.

et krydderi.explanation: "Et krydderi" means "a spice". For a fresh herb, use "en krydderurt" (a herb) instead: "Jeg dyrker krydderurter på altanen" (I grow herbs on the balcony).

sentence.da: Man bruger **krydderi** for at give mad smag.
sentence.en: You use spice to give food flavor.

et kryds.explanation: "Et kryds" means "an intersection". When you tick a box on a form, it also means "an X mark": "Sæt et kryds her" (Put an X here).

sentence.da: Drej til venstre i det næste **kryds**.
sentence.en: Turn left at the next intersection.

et krydstogt.explanation: "Et krydstogt" means "a cruise". To say you go on one, use "at tage på krydstogt" (to go on a cruise): "Vi tager på krydstogt i sommer" (We are going on a cruise this summer).

sentence.da: På et **krydstogt** bor man på et stort skib.
sentence.en: On a cruise you live on a big ship.

et kunstværk.explanation: "Et kunstværk" means "a work of art". It is built from "kunst" (art) and "et værk" (a work).

sentence.da: Maleriet er et **kunstværk**, som mange mennesker vil se.
sentence.en: The painting is a work of art that many people want to see.

et kup.explanation: "Et kup" means "a coup or heist". When people take power by force, it means "a coup": "Hæren tog magten ved et kup" (The army took power in a coup). When a robbery is planned, it means "a heist": "Tyvene planlagde et kup" (The thieves planned a heist). When you find a bargain, use "at gøre et kup" (to get a bargain): "Jeg gjorde et kup på markedet" (I got a bargain at the market).

sentence.da: Hæren tog magten i landet ved et **kup**.
sentence.en: The army took power in the country in a coup.

et kursus.explanation: "Et kursus" means "a course". To say you attend one, use "gå på kursus" (go on a course): "Hun går på kursus i aften" (She is at a course tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **kursus** i spansk i foråret.
sentence.en: I am taking a Spanish course in the spring.

et kvadrat.explanation: "Et kvadrat" means "a square". For a town square, use "et torv" (a town square) instead: "Vi mødes på torvet" (We meet at the town square). The word is also in "kvadratmeter" (square meters). For example, "Lejligheden er firs kvadratmeter" (The apartment is eighty square meters).

sentence.da: Hun tegner et **kvadrat** med fire lige sider.
sentence.en: She draws a square with four equal sides.

et kvartal.explanation: "Et kvartal" means "a quarter (of a year)". For the block of buildings between streets in a town, it also means "a city block": "Vi bor i samme kvartal" (We live in the same block). For a part of town, use "et kvarter" (a neighborhood) instead: "Vi bor i et rart kvarter" (We live in a nice neighborhood).

sentence.da: Firmaet tjente flere penge i første **kvartal** i år end sidste år.
sentence.en: The company earned more money in the first quarter this year than last year.

et kvarter.explanation: "Et kvarter" means "a neighborhood". When you talk about time, it also means "a quarter of an hour": "Vi ses om et kvarter" (See you in fifteen minutes).

sentence.da: Vi bor i et rart **kvarter** tæt på centrum.
sentence.en: We live in a nice neighborhood close to the center.

et kys.explanation: "Et kys" means "a kiss". It is the noun for the verb "at kysse" (to kiss). To say a man kisses a woman, use the verb: "Han kysser hende" (He kisses her).

sentence.da: Hun gav ham et **kys** på kinden.
sentence.en: She gave him a kiss on the cheek.

et kæledyr.explanation: "Et kæledyr" means "a pet". It is built from "at kæle" (to cuddle) and "et dyr" (an animal).

sentence.da: Vi har en hund som **kæledyr**.
sentence.en: We have a dog as a pet.

et kælenavn.explanation: "Et kælenavn" means "a nickname". It is built from "at kæle" (to cuddle) and "et navn" (a name). A common loving name is "skat" (sweetheart). For example, "Min mor kalder mig skat" (My mom calls me sweetheart).

sentence.da: Han bruger et **kælenavn** i stedet for hendes rigtige navn.
sentence.en: He uses a nickname instead of her real name.

et kærestepar.explanation: "Et kærestepar" means "a couple (dating)". For married people, use "et ægtepar" (a married couple) instead: "Det gamle ægtepar bor i et lille hus" (The old married couple live in a small house).

sentence.da: Det unge **kærestepar** holder hinanden i hånden.
sentence.en: The young couple is holding hands.

et kærlighedsbrev.explanation: "Et kærlighedsbrev" means "a love letter". It is built from "kærlighed" (love) and "et brev" (a letter). The part "brev" is also in "en brevkasse" (a mailbox).

sentence.da: I hans **kærlighedsbrev** stod der: Jeg elsker dig.
sentence.en: In his love letter it said: I love you.

et kærlighedsforhold.explanation: "Et kærlighedsforhold" means "a romantic relationship". It is built from "kærlighed" (love) and "et forhold" (a relationship). "Forhold" also names other kinds of relationships. For example, "et godt forhold til min chef" (a good relationship with my boss).

sentence.da: Et **kærlighedsforhold** er, når to mennesker elsker hinanden og er sammen.
sentence.en: A romantic relationship is when two people love each other and are together.

et køkken.explanation: "Et køkken" means "a kitchen". When you talk about a style of cooking, it means "cuisine": "det danske køkken" (Danish cuisine).

sentence.da: Jeg laver aftensmad i et lille **køkken**.
sentence.en: I make dinner in a small kitchen.

et køkkenbord.explanation: "Et køkkenbord" means "a kitchen table or counter". It is built from "et køkken" (a kitchen) and "et bord" (a table). When you prepare food on it, it means "a kitchen counter": "Jeg skærer brød på køkkenbordet" (I cut bread on the kitchen counter).

sentence.da: Vi spiser morgenmad ved vores **køkkenbord**.
sentence.en: We eat breakfast at our kitchen table.

et køkkenur.explanation: "Et køkkenur" means "a kitchen timer". It is built from "et køkken" (a kitchen) and "et ur" (a clock). The part "ur" also means "a watch". For example, "Min far har et nyt ur" (My dad has a new watch).

sentence.da: Jeg stillede et **køkkenur** på tyve minutter.
sentence.en: I set a kitchen timer for twenty minutes.

et køleskab.explanation: "Et køleskab" means "a fridge". It is built from "at køle" (to cool) and "et skab" (a cupboard), so it is literally a "cooling cupboard". "Skab" also ends "et klædeskab" (a wardrobe).

sentence.da: Mælk skal stå i et **køleskab**.
sentence.en: Milk must be kept in a fridge.

et køn.explanation: "Et køn" means "a gender or sex". To include everyone, say "begge køn" (both genders): "Kurset er for begge køn" (The course is for both genders).

sentence.da: På formularen skal du skrive dit **køn** og din alder.
sentence.en: On the form you must write your gender and your age.

et kønummer.explanation: "Et kønummer" means "a queue number". It is built from "en kø" (a queue) and "et nummer" (a number). To get one from the machine, use "at trække" (to pull): "Jeg trækker et kønummer" (I take a queue number).

sentence.da: Tag et **kønummer** og vent, til din tur kommer.
sentence.en: Take a queue number and wait until your turn comes.

et kørekort.explanation: "Et kørekort" means "a driver's license". To say you earn one, use "at tage kørekort" (literally "to take a driver's license"): "Jeg tager kørekort i år" (I am getting my license this year).

sentence.da: Jeg må ikke køre bil uden **kørekort**.
sentence.en: I am not allowed to drive a car without a license.

et køretøj.explanation: "Et køretøj" means "a vehicle". It comes from "at køre" (to drive). The ending "tøj" also appears in "værktøj" (tools) and "legetøj" (toys).

sentence.da: En lastbil er et stort **køretøj**.
sentence.en: A truck is a big vehicle.

kaffe.explanation: "Kaffe" means "a coffee". To order one, say "en kaffe, tak" (a coffee, please). To invite someone, ask "Skal vi have en kop kaffe?" (Shall we have a cup of coffee?).

sentence.da: **Kaffe** laves af kaffebønner og varmt vand.
sentence.en: Coffee is made from coffee beans and hot water.

kajak.explanation: "Kajak" means "kayaking". To say you go kayaking, use "at sejle i kajak" (to go by kayak): "Vi sejler i kajak på søen" (We go kayaking on the lake). When you mean the small boat, it means "a kayak": "en rød kajak" (a red kayak).

sentence.da: En **kajak** er en smal båd, og man sidder lavt i den.
sentence.en: A kayak is a narrow boat, and you sit low in it.

kakao.explanation: "Kakao" means "a cocoa". When you order the drink, it means "a hot chocolate": "En varm kakao, tak" (A hot chocolate, please).

sentence.da: Man laver **kakao** af mælk og kakaopulver.
sentence.en: You make cocoa from milk and cocoa powder.

kakaomælk.explanation: "Kakaomælk" means "chocolate milk". It is built from "kakao" (cocoa) and "mælk" (milk). For the hot drink, use "varm kakao" (hot cocoa): "En varm kakao, tak" (A hot cocoa, please).

sentence.da: **Kakaomælk** er mælk med kakao i, og børn elsker den.
sentence.en: Chocolate milk is milk with cocoa in it, and children love it.

kan du gentage det?.explanation: "Kan du gentage det?" means "Can you repeat that?". When you did not catch what someone said, ask this to hear it again. To ask more politely, add "tak" (please) at the end: "Kan du gentage det, tak?" (Can you repeat that, please?)

sentence.da: Undskyld, **kan du gentage det**?
sentence.en: Sorry, can you repeat that?

kan jeg betale med kort?.explanation: "Kan jeg betale med kort?" means "Can I pay by card?". It is built from "kan jeg" (can I), "betale" (pay), "med" (with) and "kort" (a card). To ask about a phone payment app, swap "kort" for "MobilePay": "Kan jeg betale med MobilePay?" (Can I pay with MobilePay?)

sentence.da: Hej, **kan jeg betale med kort**?
sentence.en: Hi, can I pay by card?

kan jeg købe ...?.explanation: "Kan jeg købe ...?" means "Can I buy ...?". "Kan jeg" means "can I". Say the item after "købe" (to buy): "Kan jeg købe en billet?" (Can I buy a ticket?) To ask politely in a shop or café, you can also say "Jeg vil gerne have en kaffe" (I would like a coffee).

sentence.da: Undskyld, **kan jeg købe** en kop kaffe?
sentence.en: Excuse me, can I buy a cup of coffee?

kanel.explanation: "Kanel" means "cinnamon". The word is the first part of "en kanelsnegl" (a cinnamon roll), a pastry sold in Danish bakeries.

sentence.da: Jeg putter **kanel** i min grød.
sentence.en: I put cinnamon in my porridge.

kaos.explanation: "Kaos" means "chaos". To say things are completely out of control, use "det rene kaos" (pure chaos): "Det er det rene kaos" (It is pure chaos). Spell it with a "k" and no "h".

sentence.da: Når alle råber, bliver det hurtigt til **kaos**.
sentence.en: When everyone shouts, it quickly turns into chaos.

karantæne.explanation: "En karantæne" means "a quarantine". To put people in quarantine, use "at sætte i karantæne": "Man sætter de syge i karantæne" (They put the sick people in quarantine). Spell it with a "k" and an "æ".

sentence.da: Efter rejsen skal man være i **karantæne** i ti dage.
sentence.en: After the trip, you must be in quarantine for ten days.

karry.explanation: "Karry" means "curry". The powder is called "karrypulver" (curry powder). For example, "Jeg køber karrypulver" (I buy curry powder).

sentence.da: **Karry** er et gult krydderi til indisk mad.
sentence.en: Curry is a yellow spice for Indian food.

kartofler.explanation: "Kartofler" means "potatoes", the plural of "en kartoffel" (a potato). To say how potatoes are cooked, put a word in front: "kogte kartofler" (boiled potatoes).

sentence.da: Pommes frites er lavet af **kartofler**.
sentence.en: French fries are made of potatoes.

kattemad.explanation: "Kattemad" means "cat food". It is built from "en kat" (a cat) and "mad" (food). The part "mad" also builds "morgenmad" (breakfast) and "aftensmad" (dinner).

sentence.da: **Kattemad** er mad til katte, ikke til mennesker.
sentence.en: Cat food is food for cats, not for people.

ked af.explanation: "Ked af" means "sorry or sad". It is used after "er" (is): "Hun er ked af det" (She is sad). To say sorry after bumping into someone, use "undskyld" (sorry, excuse me) instead: "Undskyld, jeg ramte dig" (Sorry, I bumped into you).

forms.en: I am sorry. / I am sad.

forms.da: Jeg er ked af, at jeg kom for sent.
forms.en: I am sorry that I came too late.

sentence.da: Hun græder og er **ked af** det.
sentence.en: She is crying and she is sad.

ked af det.explanation: "Ked af det" means "sad". To say you are not sad, put "ikke" (not) before "ked": "Jeg er ikke ked af det" (I am not sad). When you say sorry for something you did, it also means "sorry": "Jeg er ked af, at jeg kom for sent" (I am sorry that I came late).

sentence.da: Barnet græder og er **ked af det**.
sentence.en: The child is crying and is sad.

kedelig.explanation: "Kedelig" means "boring". When something is a pity, it means "unfortunate": "Det er kedeligt" (That is too bad). To say you yourself are bored, use "Jeg keder mig" (I am bored) instead.

sentence.da: Filmen er **kedelig**, og jeg gaber.
sentence.en: The film is boring, and I am yawning.

kedsomhed.explanation: "En kedsomhed" means "boredom". For the thing that is boring, use "kedelig" (boring) instead: "Filmen er kedelig" (The film is boring).

sentence.da: Når regnen holder os inde, melder **kedsomhed** sig hurtigt.
sentence.en: When the rain keeps us inside, boredom soon shows up.

kemi.explanation: "Kemi" means "chemistry". As a school subject, Danish uses it with no article. For example, "Vi har kemi på torsdag" (We have chemistry on Thursday).

sentence.da: I **kemi** laver vi forsøg i laboratoriet.
sentence.en: In chemistry we do experiments in the lab.

kemisk.explanation: "Kemisk" means "chemical". To say clothes are taken to be cleaned without water, use "kemisk rensning" (dry cleaning): "Jeg afleverer jakken til kemisk rensning" (I am dropping the jacket off for dry cleaning).

sentence.da: Rust er en **kemisk** reaktion mellem jern og ilt.
sentence.en: Rust is a chemical reaction between iron and oxygen.

kendskab.explanation: "Et kendskab" means "knowledge", as in being familiar with a place or a subject. To say you know something well, use "til" (of) after it: "Jeg har godt kendskab til byen" (I have good knowledge of the city). For facts you have learned, use "viden" (knowledge) instead: "Hun har stor viden om historie" (She has great knowledge of history).

sentence.da: Hun har godt **kendskab** til dansk historie.
sentence.en: She has good knowledge of Danish history.

kendt.explanation: "Kendt" means "famous". To say what someone is known for, it also means "known", with "for" (for) after it: "Hun er kendt for sin musik" (She is known for her music).

sentence.da: Hun er **kendt**, og alle i landet kender hende.
sentence.en: She is famous, and everyone in the country knows her.

ketchup.explanation: "Ketchup" means "ketchup". To ask for some, put "noget" (some) before it: "Jeg vil gerne have noget ketchup" (I would like some ketchup).

sentence.da: Vil du have **ketchup** til pommes frites?
sentence.en: Do you want ketchup with the fries?

kikærter.explanation: "Kikærter" means "chickpeas". The word is plural. To talk about one, use "en kikært" (a chickpea).

sentence.da: Hummus er lavet af **kikærter**, olie og hvidløg.
sentence.en: Hummus is made of chickpeas, oil and garlic.

kina.explanation: "Kina" means "China". Spell it with a "K" and no "h". To say you travel there, use "til" (to): "Jeg rejser til Kina" (I am traveling to China).

sentence.da: **Kina** er et stort land i Asien.
sentence.en: China is a big country in Asia.

kinesisk.explanation: "Kinesisk" means "Chinese". Danish does not capitalize it, unlike English. For example, "kinesisk mad" (Chinese food). For the language, use it alone: "Jeg taler kinesisk" (I speak Chinese).

sentence.da: I Kina taler man **kinesisk**.
sentence.en: In China, people speak Chinese.

klam.explanation: "Klam" means "clammy". When something feels cold and sticky, use it: "en klam hånd" (a clammy hand). When you find something disgusting, it also means "gross": "Det er så klamt" (That is so gross).

sentence.da: Efter regnen var tøjet **klam** og koldt.
sentence.en: After the rain, the clothes were clammy and cold.

klar.explanation: "Klar" means "clear". When someone is prepared, it also means "ready": "Er du klar?" (Are you ready?) To answer "of course", say "Det er klart" (Of course). Do not mix it up with "færdig" (finished). For example, "Jeg er færdig" (I am finished).

sentence.da: Maden er **klar**, og vi kan spise.
sentence.en: The food is ready, and we can eat.

klassisk.explanation: "Klassisk" means "classic". To call something a lasting favorite, put it before the noun: "en klassisk bil" (a classic car). When you talk about music, it also means "classical": "klassisk musik" (classical music).

sentence.da: Mozart og Beethoven skrev **klassisk** musik.
sentence.en: Mozart and Beethoven wrote classical music.

klatring.explanation: "En klatring" means "climbing". It is the noun for the verb "at klatre" (to climb).

forms.en: I do climbing as a sport.

sentence.da: Til **klatring** bruger man reb, sele og klatresko.
sentence.en: For climbing you use a rope, a harness and climbing shoes.

klimaforandring.explanation: "En klimaforandring" means "a climate change". It is built from "klima" (climate) and "en forandring" (a change). To talk about the global problem, use the plural "klimaforandringer": "Vi taler om klimaforandringer" (We are talking about climate changes).

sentence.da: Den globale **klimaforandring** får havene til at stige.
sentence.en: The global climate change makes the oceans rise.

klimapolitik.explanation: "En klimapolitik" means "a climate policy". It is built from "klima" (climate) and "en politik" (a policy). To name one party's, put the party before it: "partiets klimapolitik" (the party's climate policy).

sentence.da: Regeringens **klimapolitik** skal sænke Danmarks udledning af drivhusgasser.
sentence.en: The government's climate policy must lower Denmark's emissions of greenhouse gases.

klodset.explanation: "Klodset" means "clumsy". To say someone put words badly, use it for what they said: "Det var en klodset bemærkning" (That was a clumsy remark).

sentence.da: Han taber ofte koppen, fordi han er så **klodset**.
sentence.en: He often drops the cup because he is so clumsy.

klog.explanation: "Klog" means "wise". For a person who thinks well, it also means "smart": "Hun er meget klog for sin alder" (She is very smart for her age). To say something was a mistake, say "Det var ikke særlig klogt" (That was not very smart).

sentence.da: Hun er meget **klog** for sin alder.
sentence.en: She is very smart for her age.

klokken.explanation: "Klokken" means "o'clock". Literally, it means "the clock". To tell the time, say "Klokken er tre" (It is three o'clock). To say when something happens, say "Vi mødes klokken otte" (We meet at eight o'clock). In writing, it is shortened to "kl."

sentence.da: **Klokken** er otte om morgenen.
sentence.en: It is eight o'clock in the morning.

klokken er fem.explanation: "Klokken er fem" means "It's five o'clock". To ask the time, say "Hvad er klokken?" (What time is it?) and the answer starts with "klokken er". Danish counts half hours toward the next hour. For example, "halv tre" (literally "half three") means half past two, as in "Klokken er halv tre" (It is half past two).

sentence.da: **Klokken er fem** nu.
sentence.en: It's five o'clock now.

knapt.explanation: "Knapt" means "barely". To say something hardly happened at all, add "nok" (enough): "Han har knapt nok sovet" (He has hardly slept at all).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **knapt** høre dig, for musikken er for høj.
sentence.en: I can barely hear you because the music is too loud.

knust.explanation: "Knust" means "heartbroken". For a person who is very sad, use it: "Hun er knust efter nyheden" (She is heartbroken after the news). For things, it means "smashed": "Glasset var knust" (The glass was smashed).

sentence.da: Hun var **knust**, da han forlod hende.
sentence.en: She was heartbroken when he left her.

knækbrød.explanation: "Et knækbrød" means "a crispbread". It comes from "at knække" (to snap), because it snaps when you break it.

sentence.da: Man kan smøre smør og ost på et **knækbrød**.
sentence.en: You can spread butter and cheese on a crispbread.

kobber.explanation: "Kobber" means "copper". For a wire made of copper, add "tråd" (wire): "Jeg har købt en rulle kobbertråd" (I bought a roll of copper wire).

sentence.da: Elektriske ledninger er ofte lavet af **kobber**.
sentence.en: Electric wires are often made of copper.

kogt.explanation: "Kogt" means "boiled". It comes from the verb "at koge" (to boil). Do not mix it up with "stegt" (fried). For example, "en stegt kartoffel" (a fried potato).

sentence.da: Kartoflen er **kogt** i varmt vand.
sentence.en: The potato is boiled in hot water.

kokain.explanation: "Kokain" means "cocaine". Spell it with a "k" in place of both "c" letters: "kokain".

sentence.da: Det er ulovligt at købe og sælge **kokain**.
sentence.en: It is illegal to buy and sell cocaine.

kold.explanation: "Kold" means "cold". To say you feel cold, say: "Jeg fryser" (I am freezing).

sentence.da: Det er en **kold** dag, og jeg fryser.
sentence.en: It is a cold day, and I am freezing.

kolesterol.explanation: "Kolesterol" means "cholesterol". To say you have too much of it, say: "Jeg har højt kolesterol" (I have high cholesterol).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at for højt **kolesterol** kan skade hjertet.
sentence.en: The doctor says that too high cholesterol can harm the heart.

kom nu.explanation: "Kom nu" means "come on". Literally, it is "come now". To encourage someone: "Kom nu, du kan godt!" (Come on, you can do it!). To say you do not believe what someone said: "Kom nu, det passer ikke!" (Come on, that is not true!).

forms.da: Kom nu, vi skal af sted.
forms.en: Come on, we have to go.

sentence.da: **Kom nu**, bussen kører snart!
sentence.en: Come on, the bus leaves soon!

kommende.explanation: "Kommende" means "upcoming". It comes from the verb "at komme" (to come). To talk about the next weekend, say: "den kommende weekend" (the coming weekend). To talk about people who will soon work with you: "mine kommende kolleger" (my future colleagues).

sentence.da: Vi har et **kommende** møde på mandag.
sentence.en: We have an upcoming meeting on Monday.

kommunikation.explanation: "En kommunikation" means "a communication". To say a team needs to talk and understand each other better: "Vi har brug for bedre kommunikation" (We need better communication). It comes from the verb "at kommunikere" (to communicate).

sentence.da: God **kommunikation** i teamet gør arbejdet lettere for alle.
sentence.en: Good communication in the team makes work easier for everyone.

kompetent.explanation: "Kompetent" means "competent". To describe good help from someone who knows the work, say: "kompetent hjælp" (competent help).

sentence.da: Lægen er meget **kompetent** og forklarer tingene godt.
sentence.en: The doctor is very competent and explains things well.

kompleks.explanation: "Kompleks" means "complex". To describe a problem with many causes, say: "Problemet er kompleks" (The problem is complex). To say something is complicated, use "kompliceret" (complicated): "Opskriften er kompliceret" (The recipe is complicated).

sentence.da: Sagen er **kompleks**, fordi mange mennesker er involveret.
sentence.en: The case is complex because many people are involved.
