komplet.explanation: "Komplet" means "complete". To say something is entirely so, use it before an adjective: "komplet umuligt" (completely impossible).

sentence.da: Vi har nu et **komplet** sæt tallerkener.
sentence.en: We now have a complete set of plates.

kompliceret.explanation: "Kompliceret" means "complicated". It comes from the verb "at komplicere" (to complicate). To say something is not hard, say: "Det er ikke så kompliceret" (It is not that complicated).

sentence.da: Det er en **kompliceret** situation, og ingen forstår den.
sentence.en: It is a complicated situation, and no one understands it.

kompost.explanation: "En kompost" means "compost". It also means the heap or bin where scraps rot. To say where food scraps go, say: "Madaffald kommer i komposten" (Food scraps go in the compost).

sentence.da: Kartoffelskræller og blade kan blive til **kompost** i haven.
sentence.en: Potato peels and leaves can turn into compost in the garden.

koncentreret.explanation: "Koncentreret" means "focused". It comes from the verb "at koncentrere sig" (to concentrate). For example, "Jeg koncentrerer mig" (I am concentrating). For a drink with little water in it, it means "concentrated": "koncentreret saft" (concentrated juice).

sentence.da: Han sidder **koncentreret** og læser hele eftermiddagen.
sentence.en: He sits focused and reads all afternoon.

kondition.explanation: "Kondition" means "fitness". To say you are out of shape, say: "Jeg har dårlig kondition" (I am out of shape). Do not use it for the state of an object, as English "condition" can. For that, use "tilstand" (condition): "bilens tilstand" (the condition of the car).

sentence.da: Jeg løber hver dag for at få bedre **kondition**.
sentence.en: I run every day to improve my fitness.

konfetti.explanation: "Konfetti" means "confetti". This word has no article. To say you throw it at a celebration, say: "Vi kaster konfetti" (We throw confetti).

sentence.da: Brudeparret fik **konfetti** over hovedet.
sentence.en: The bride and groom got confetti over their heads.

kongelig.explanation: "Kongelig" means "royal". In Denmark, a famous theater has it in its name. For example, "Det Kongelige Teater" (The Royal Danish Theater).

sentence.da: Hun er **kongelig** og bor på Amalienborg i København.
sentence.en: She is royal and lives at Amalienborg in Copenhagen.

konkret.explanation: "Konkret" means "concrete", as in clear and specific. To ask for a clear suggestion, say: "et konkret forslag" (a specific proposal). Do not mix it up with the building material, which is "beton" (concrete). For example, "Muren er af beton" (The wall is made of concrete).

sentence.da: Kan du give et **konkret** eksempel, så jeg forstår det?
sentence.en: Can you give a concrete example so that I understand it?

konkurs.explanation: "Konkurs" means "bankrupt". To say a company ran out of money and closed, say: "Firmaet gik konkurs" (The company went bankrupt). The phrase is "at gå konkurs" (to go bankrupt).

sentence.da: Butikken måtte lukke, fordi ejeren ikke kunne betale og var **konkurs**.
sentence.en: The shop had to close because the owner could not pay and was bankrupt.

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er meget **konservativ** og kan ikke lide forandringer.
sentence.en: My grandfather is very conservative and does not like changes.

konstant.explanation: "Konstant" means "constant". To say a noise never stops, say: "Der er konstant larm" (There is constant noise). To say a value does not change, say: "en konstant temperatur" (a constant temperature).

sentence.da: Telefonen ringer **konstant**, og det stopper aldrig.
sentence.en: The phone rings constantly, and it never stops.

kontant.explanation: "Kontant" means "cash". To say you pay by card instead, say: "Jeg betaler med kort" (I pay by card).

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke kort og betaler **kontant**.
sentence.en: I have no card and pay in cash.

kontanthjælp.explanation: "Kontanthjælp" means "welfare". In Denmark the municipality ("kommunen") pays it. It is built from "kontant" (cash) and "hjælp" (help).

sentence.da: Hun får **kontanthjælp**, når hun hverken har job eller penge.
sentence.en: She gets welfare when she has neither a job nor money.

korrekt.explanation: "Korrekt" means "correct". To confirm that someone has it right, say: "Det er korrekt" (That is correct).

sentence.da: Du får point, fordi dit svar er **korrekt**.
sentence.en: You get points because your answer is correct.

korrupt.explanation: "Korrupt" means "corrupt". The noun is "korruption" (corruption). To say a country has this problem, say: "Der er korruption i landet" (There is corruption in the country).

sentence.da: Dommeren tog imod penge og var derfor **korrupt**.
sentence.en: The judge accepted money and was therefore corrupt.

kort.explanation: "Kort" means "short". To say a day is short, say: "Dagen er kort" (The day is short). Do not mix it up with "et kort" (a card or a map). For example, "et kort over byen" (a map of the city).

sentence.da: Hans hår er **kort**, ikke langt.
sentence.en: His hair is short, not long.

kort sagt.explanation: "Kort sagt" means "in short". It is built from "kort" (short) and "sagt" (said). Literally, it is "short said".

sentence.da: **Kort sagt**, jeg kan ikke komme i morgen.
sentence.en: In short, I cannot come tomorrow.

kortvarig.explanation: "Kortvarig" means "brief". It is built from "kort" (short) and "varig" (lasting).

sentence.da: Smerten var **kortvarig**, og efter en time var den væk.
sentence.en: The pain was short-lived, and after an hour it was gone.

kostbar.explanation: "Kostbar" means "costly". To say memories matter greatly to you, say: "kostbare minder" (precious memories).

sentence.da: Vi må ikke spilde tiden, fordi den er **kostbar**.
sentence.en: We must not waste time because it is precious.

kraftig.explanation: "Kraftig" means "strong", as in powerful, such as wind, rain or a blow. To describe a heavily built body, say: "en kraftig mand" (a heavily built man). To describe someone with strong muscles, use "stærk" (strong): "Han er stærk" (He is strong).

sentence.da: Der var **kraftig** regn hele natten, så gaden stod under vand.
sentence.en: There was heavy rain all night, so the street was flooded.

kraftigt.explanation: "Kraftigt" means "heavily". It comes from the adjective "kraftig" (strong). To say a price or a value dropped a lot, say: "Valutaen faldt kraftigt" (The currency fell sharply).

sentence.da: Priserne steg **kraftigt**, og mange har svært ved at betale.
sentence.en: Prices rose sharply, and many have trouble paying.

kreativ.explanation: "Kreativ" means "creative". To say a way of solving a problem is new and clever, say: "en kreativ løsning" (a creative solution).

sentence.da: Hun er **kreativ** og tegner mange flotte billeder.
sentence.en: She is creative and draws many nice pictures.

kreativitet.explanation: "Kreativitet" means "creativity". It is the noun for the adjective "kreativ" (creative). To say a task needs new ideas, say: "Vi har brug for kreativitet i løsningen" (We need creativity in the solution).

sentence.da: Børn har masser af **kreativitet**, når de tegner og leger.
sentence.en: Children have lots of creativity when they draw and play.

kredit.explanation: "En kredit" means "a credit", as in paying later. To say a shop does not let you pay later, say: "Butikken giver ikke kredit" (The shop does not give credit).

sentence.da: Hun købte sofaen på **kredit** og betaler hver måned.
sentence.en: She bought the sofa on credit and pays every month.

kriminalitet.explanation: "Kriminalitet" means "crime", about crime in general. To say there is little crime in a place, say: "Der er lidt kriminalitet her" (There is little crime here). To talk about one act, use "en forbrydelse" (a crime): "Tyveriet var en forbrydelse" (The theft was a crime).

sentence.da: Der er meget lidt **kriminalitet** i vores lille by.
sentence.en: There is very little crime in our small town.

kriminel.explanation: "Kriminel" means "criminal". To describe behavior that breaks the law, say: "kriminel adfærd" (criminal behavior). To name the person, use "en kriminel" (a criminal).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en **kriminel** bande i byen.
sentence.en: The police found a criminal gang in the city.

kristen.explanation: "Kristen" means "Christian". To name a person who follows this faith, say: "en kristen" (a Christian).

sentence.da: Hun er **kristen** og går i kirke hver søndag.
sentence.en: She is Christian and goes to church every Sunday.

kristendom.explanation: "Kristendom" means "Christianity". It comes from the word "kristen" (Christian). This word has no article, so leave out "en". For example, "Jeg læser om kristendom" (I am reading about Christianity).

sentence.da: **Kristendom** er den største religion i Danmark.
sentence.en: Christianity is the biggest religion in Denmark.

kritik.explanation: "Kritik" means "criticism". This word has no article, so leave out "en". For example, "Der kom meget kritik" (There was a lot of criticism).

forms.en: He got a lot of criticism.

sentence.da: Hun fik meget **kritik** for sin tale.
sentence.en: She got a lot of criticism for her speech.

kritisk.explanation: "Kritisk" means "critical". When you judge something carefully, use it: "kritisk tænkning" (critical thinking). When a situation is serious or dangerous, use it: "en kritisk situation" (a critical situation).

sentence.da: Man skal være **kritisk**, når man læser nyheder på nettet.
sentence.en: You should be critical when you read news online.

krudt.explanation: "Krudt" means "gunpowder". To say someone is not very clever, Danes say: "Han har ikke opfundet krudtet" (He did not invent gunpowder).

sentence.da: Fyrværkeri indeholder **krudt**, og det brænder meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: Fireworks contain gunpowder, and it burns very fast.

krydderier.explanation: "Et krydderi" means "a spice". To talk about more than one, use the plural: "Jeg køber krydderier" (I am buying spices). Do not mix it up with "en urt" (a herb). For example, "Basilikum er en urt" (Basil is a herb).

sentence.da: Kanel og karry er **krydderier**.
sentence.en: Cinnamon and curry are spices.

krydret.explanation: "Krydret" means "spicy". For food that burns your mouth, like chili, use "stærk" (hot): "Maden er for stærk" (The food is too hot).

sentence.da: Karry og peber gør maden **krydret**.
sentence.en: Curry and pepper make the food spicy.

kræft.explanation: "Kræft" means "cancer". To name the kind, put the body part in front: "hudkræft" (skin cancer).

sentence.da: Hun havde **kræft**, men blev rask efter behandlingen.
sentence.en: She had cancer but got well after the treatment.

krøllet.explanation: "Krøllet" means "curly". When a shirt or a paper is not smooth, it means "wrinkled": "Skjorten er krøllet" (The shirt is wrinkled).

sentence.da: Min lillesøster har **krøllet** hår, mens jeg har lige hår.
sentence.en: My little sister has curly hair, while I have straight hair.

kul.explanation: "Kul" means "coal". To talk about charcoal for a grill, put "træ" (wood) in front: "trækul" (charcoal).

sentence.da: Før i tiden fyrede man i ovnen med **kul** for at få varme.
sentence.en: In the past people fired the stove with coal to get warmth.

kulde.explanation: "Kulde" means "cold". To say you cannot stand the low temperature, say: "Jeg kan ikke tåle kulde" (I cannot stand the cold). To describe a thing, use "kold" (cold): "koldt vand" (cold water).

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der sne og **kulde**.
sentence.en: In winter there is snow and cold.

kulhydrat.explanation: "Et kulhydrat" means "a carbohydrate". To talk about carbohydrates in general, use the plural: "Brød indeholder kulhydrater" (Bread contains carbohydrates).

sentence.da: Der er meget **kulhydrat** i pasta og ris.
sentence.en: There is a lot of carbohydrate in pasta and rice.

kulstof.explanation: "Kulstof" means "carbon". It is built from "kul" (coal) and "stof" (substance), so literally "coal stuff".

sentence.da: Planter og dyr består blandt andet af **kulstof**.
sentence.en: Plants and animals consist partly of carbon.

kun.explanation: "Kun" means "only". To say nobody else knows something, say: "Kun jeg ved det" (Only I know it). To say that is all you know, say: "Jeg ved kun det" (I only know that).

sentence.da: Jeg har **kun** to kroner.
sentence.en: I only have two kroner.

kundeservice.explanation: "Kundeservice" means "customer service". It is built from "en kunde" (a customer) and "service".

sentence.da: Jeg ringede til **kundeservice**, men ingen svarede.
sentence.en: I called customer service, but nobody answered.

kundskab.explanation: "En kundskab" means "knowledge". To talk about what someone knows, use the plural: "gode kundskaber i matematik" (good knowledge of math).

sentence.da: Lægen har stor **kundskab** om kroppen og sygdomme.
sentence.en: The doctor has great knowledge about the body and diseases.

kunst.explanation: "Kunst" means "art". To name one work, say "et kunstværk" (a work of art). To name the person who makes it, say "en kunstner" (an artist).

sentence.da: Hun elsker **kunst** og maler hver weekend.
sentence.en: She loves art and paints every weekend.

kunstig intelligens.explanation: "Kunstig intelligens" means "artificial intelligence". It is built from "kunstig" (artificial) and "intelligens" (intelligence). The short form is "AI".

sentence.da: Mange bruger **kunstig intelligens** til at skrive tekster.
sentence.en: Many people use artificial intelligence to write texts.

kvalificeret.explanation: "Kvalificeret" means "qualified". To say a guess rests on real knowledge, say: "et kvalificeret gæt" (an informed guess).

sentence.da: Hun er **kvalificeret** til jobbet, fordi hun har studeret i fem år.
sentence.en: She is qualified for the job because she has studied for five years.

kvalm.explanation: "Kvalm" means "nauseous". Do not use "syg" (sick) for this feeling, because it means ill with a disease: "Jeg er syg" (I am sick).

sentence.da: Jeg er **kvalm**, og jeg har ondt i maven.
sentence.en: I am nauseous and my stomach hurts.

kvalme.explanation: "En kvalme" means "nausea". To say something disgusts you, say: "Det giver mig kvalme" (It makes me sick).

sentence.da: Efter turen på båden fik jeg **kvalme** og måtte sidde ned.
sentence.en: After the boat trip I felt nauseous and had to sit down.

kvart.explanation: "Kvart" means "quarter". To talk about fifteen minutes of time, use "et kvarter" (a quarter of an hour): "Vi venter et kvarter" (We wait a quarter of an hour).

sentence.da: Vi ses **kvart** over tre.
sentence.en: See you at a quarter past three.

kvart i.explanation: "Kvart i" means "quarter to". To say when something starts, say: "Mødet begynder kvart i ni" (The meeting begins at a quarter to nine). Do not mix it up with "kvart over" (quarter past). For example, "Mødet begynder kvart over ni" (The meeting begins at a quarter past nine).

sentence.da: Filmen starter **kvart i** syv.
sentence.en: The movie starts at a quarter to seven.

kvart over.explanation: "Kvart over" means "quarter past". To say when something starts, say: "Mødet begynder kvart over ni" (The meeting begins at a quarter past nine). Do not mix it up with "kvart i" (quarter to). For example, "Mødet begynder kvart i ni" (The meeting begins at a quarter to nine).

sentence.da: Bussen kommer **kvart over** otte.
sentence.en: The bus comes at a quarter past eight.

kvik.explanation: "Kvik" means "quick-witted". To describe speed of movement, use "hurtig" (fast): "en hurtig bil" (a fast car).

sentence.da: Hun er **kvik** og forstår det med det samme.
sentence.en: She is quick and understands it right away.

sentence.da: Min læge er **kvindelig**, ikke mandlig.
sentence.en: My doctor is female, not male.

kvit.explanation: "Kvit" means "even". To say you got rid of something, use "blive kvit med" (to get rid of): "Jeg vil blive kvit med min forkølelse" (I want to get rid of my cold).

sentence.da: Nu har jeg betalt min gæld, og vi er **kvit**.
sentence.en: Now I have paid my debt and we are even.

kvæg.explanation: "Kvæg" means "cattle". This word has no article, so leave out "et". For example, "Vi har kvæg på gården" (We have cattle on the farm). To name one animal, say "en ko" (a cow) or "en tyr" (a bull).

sentence.da: Landmanden har hundrede stykker **kvæg** på marken.
sentence.en: The farmer has a hundred head of cattle in the field.

kylling.explanation: "En kylling" means "a chicken". To talk about the meat, leave out "en": "kylling med ris" (chicken with rice).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **kylling** til aftensmad.
sentence.en: We are eating chicken for dinner.

kål.explanation: "En kål" means "a cabbage". To name a kind, put a color in front: "hvidkål" (white cabbage) or "rødkål" (red cabbage).

sentence.da: **Kål** er en grøn grøntsag med mange blade.
sentence.en: Cabbage is a green vegetable with many leaves.

kær.explanation: "Kær" means "dear". To start a letter, write: "Kære Anna" (Dear Anna). To address a group, write: "Kære alle" (Dear everyone).

sentence.da: Han er en **kær** ven, og jeg savner ham.
sentence.en: He is a dear friend, and I miss him.

kærlig.explanation: "Kærlig" means "loving". To end a letter warmly, write: "Kærlig hilsen" (With love).

sentence.da: Min bedstemor er altid så **kærlig** mod os.
sentence.en: My grandmother is always so loving toward us.

kærlighed.explanation: "Kærlighed" means "love". To say "I love you", use the verb "at elske" (to love): "Jeg elsker dig" (I love you).

sentence.da: Mor viser sin **kærlighed** med et kram.
sentence.en: Mom shows her love with a hug.

kærnemælk.explanation: "Kærnemælk" means "buttermilk". It is built from "kærne" (churn) and "mælk" (milk).

sentence.da: **Kærnemælk** smager surt, men jeg kan godt lide den.
sentence.en: Buttermilk tastes sour, but I like it.

kød.explanation: "Kød" means "meat". To name the kind, put an animal in front: "oksekød" (beef) or "svinekød" (pork).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser gerne **kød** og fisk.
sentence.en: I like eating meat and fish.

kølig.explanation: "Kølig" means "cool". For weather that is truly cold, use "kold" (cold): "Vandet er koldt" (The water is cold).

sentence.da: Jeg tog en jakke på, fordi aftenen var **kølig**.
sentence.en: I put on a jacket because the evening was cool.

køn.explanation: "Køn" means "pretty". To call a garden pretty, say: "Haven er køn" (The garden is pretty). Do not mix it up with "et køn" (gender). For example, "Hvilket køn har barnet?" (What gender is the child?).

sentence.da: Hun er en **køn** pige med langt hår.
sentence.en: She is a pretty girl with long hair.
